All the Details on Hailey Bieber’s Viral Blue K-Beauty Sheet Mask

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, hailey Bieber does not play about her skin care.
  • Industry observers note that jennifer Seo, head concierge at Aneue, a bespoke beauty and wellness travel concierge, immediately ID’d the mask and knows the brand well.
  • Bieber is wearing the Pyderin Hydrovuster PDRN SOS Hyal Soothing Mask, which is part of the brand’s Hydrovuster line.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, hailey Bieber does not play about her skin care. The Rhode Skin founder recently posted a now-viral Instagram carousel showing the many masks she uses to treat her skin. Among the mix of traditional sheet masks, LED devices, rubber masks, and traditional creams was one standout—a blue sheet mask that has sent the internet down a rabbit hole. But of course we’re skin care sleuths, and we gathered all the details, including its benefits and where to buy it.

Industry observers note that jennifer Seo, head concierge at Aneue, a bespoke beauty and wellness travel concierge, immediately ID’d the mask and knows the brand well. She tells ELLE the mask is from Korean skin care brand Pyderin and that its PDRN Lift Cream is the most reordered product among her clients.

Bieber is wearing the Pyderin Hydrovuster PDRN SOS Hyal Soothing Mask, which is part of the brand’s Hydrovuster line. Seo indicates the lineup was developed as a hydrating, calming collection to soothe post-treatment skin or sensitive, reactive skin. The blue tint isn’t just for aesthetic purposes either; it comes from blue azulene, an anti-inflammatory and calming ingredient that also reduces redness. Dr. Chang Son, a board-certified dermatologist based in NYC, says that its main benefit is hydration. “There may also be an immediate soothing benefit, particularly for skin following sun exposure or experiencing irritation, along with a potential instant cooling effect that leaves the skin feeling refreshed and comforted,” Son explains.

What sets this mask apart from other sheet masks is that it’s soaked in a pharmaceutical-grade serum packed with PDRN in its highest purity. “[The treatment] is highly concentrated and synergizes well with blue azulene and mucin to heal and soothe the skin,” claims Seo. The mask uses domestic PDRN extracted from Korean salmon, versus other brands that may use internationally sourced PDRN not from salmon, but from other types of fish, and may contain contaminants. “We have seen other sources of PDRN versus the raw PDRN that is used in Pyderin’s products, and there is a difference in the texture, scent, and color of this active ingredient,” Seo notes.

Son adds that the sodium PDRN used in this mask is more water-soluble, making it better suited for topical applications and easier to incorporate into skin care products such as creams and sheet masks. “Its primary role in topical formulations is hydration, although it is generally not considered as biologically active as injectable forms of PDRN,” indicates Son.

In addition to its purity, Pyderin uses a 99 percent pure source of PDRN that is also a small enough size, at 97 kilodaltons, to penetrate the skin. “If the particle size is too large, the ingredient will merely sit on top of the skin, whereas this PDRN product will penetrate the epidermis,” Seo explains.

Son and Seo agree that the combo of pure PDRN and blue azulene can be used regularly and is suitable for all skin types and skin tones, especially after skin treatments when skin can be sensitive or irritated. “I think it would be most beneficial for patients with chronic dry or inflamed skin like rosacea,” Son notes. “I generally do not recommend facial masks for patients with conditions involving significant epidermal barrier damage, such as severe eczema or cystic acne, as these may further irritate compromised skin.”.

The mask is presently sold out, but according to a Pyderin IG post, it’ll be available via Amazon in mid-to-late November, so any day now.

Latest Update: Mussels With Garlicky Miso Broth

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (388 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that mussels deserve your attention on weeknights.
  • The seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home.
  • More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that mussels deserve your attention on weeknights. An affordable and accessible protein, they also happen to cook in less time than it takes to boil water. As the bivalves steam, they release a briny liquid, further perfuming the buttery, sake-fortified miso broth. Load up each bowl with a few good ladles, slurping every drop with an assist from crusty bread or warm rice. And why not enjoy the rest of the bottle of sake alongside your meal?

The seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home. Discard any with cracked shells. Gently tap open raw mussels on a counter to see if they slowly close; if they do, those are okay to use. Swish them in a water-filled salad spinner or colander fitted inside a bowl, draining and refilling until water runs clear (give any especially dirty ones a scrub with a sponge). Use a towel to pull off the fibrous beard and set on a towel-lined tray in the fridge until you’re ready to cook.

More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.

Place 2 Tbsp. scallions from 8 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal, in a small bowl and set aside for serving.

It has been revealed that melt 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add 8 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining scallions to pot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp. white miso paste and ½ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until miso is broken up and incorporated into butter, about 20 seconds. Pour in 1 cup dry sake or dry white wine and stir to combine, then add 3–3½ lb. mussels, scrubbed, debearded. Cover pot and increase heat to medium-high. Cook, shaking pot occasionally, until mussels open, 5–7 minutes (discard any that do not open). Remove pot from heat.

Recent findings suggest that squeeze 1 lemon half over mussels. Cut remaining 1 lemon half into wedges for serving. Taste broth and season with kosher salt if needed.

Ladle mussels and broth among shallow bowls, then scatter reserved scallions over. Serve with country-style bread or steamed white rice if desired and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

#134843. “It Was Never About Fashion”: Emily in Paris’s Costume Designer Reveals the Method to Her Madness

“It Was Never About Fashion”: Emily in Paris’s Costume Designer Reveals the Method to Her Madness

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1144 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, emily in Paris premiered when audiences needed it most.
  • The love for Emily in Paris was anything but unanimous.
  • In a recent development, for six seasons, Fitoussi curated a wardrobe fit for Emily, a bright-eyed young woman unafraid to try something new, to break the rules.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, emily in Paris premiered when audiences needed it most. The Netflix original, created by Sex and the City producer Darren Star, offered an escapist fantasy: a young girl trying to find love and success in Paris in October 2020. The show functioned as a reprieve from the pandemic, a dreamy alternative in which we could vicariously live through Emily (Lily Collins) as she gallivanted around the City of Light. It was and still is delectably digestible television.

The love for Emily in Paris was anything but unanimous. Critics wasted no time tearing the show apart, with some targeting its depictions of French culture or claiming the script lacked the bite of Star’s previous television indicates. The criticism extended to Emily’s idiosyncratic wardrobe, with some writing that the clothing leaned hard on American stereotypes of French fashion or looked cartoonish, with clashing patterns and bright colors. Costume designer Marylin Fitoussi took these criticisms head-on and doubled down. Emily’s outfits weren’t meant to be couture or designer; they were meant to dress a girl finding her sense of self, expressing her desire to explore the unknown.

In a recent development, for six seasons, Fitoussi curated a wardrobe fit for Emily, a bright-eyed young woman unafraid to try something new, to break the rules. This mirrors Fitoussi’s personal philosophy on clothing: that fashion is meant to break rules, to push boundaries, to provide a space of unrelenting experimentation. Ahead of the sixth season, SCAD FASH Museum of Fashion + Film compiles six seasons’ worth of outfits in “Emily in Paris: Fashion Without Rules,” on view through March 14, 2027. The exhibition lives up to its name; for the designer, clothing is a mode of expression that lets anyone feel free, wherever they are. It offers a character study, tracing Emily’s evolution from a doe-eyed expat to a well-versed Parisian resident. (And worry not, there are also looks from Emily’s chic boss Sylvie—played with devastating elegance by Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu.).

Ahead of season 6, Bazaar sat down with Fitoussi at SCAD Fashion in Atlanta to discuss working with Lily Collins, her swan song for Emily in Paris, and how everyone has the potential for creativity.

In a recent development, marylin Fitoussi: I don’t recall a contemporary TV show being in the spotlight in this way. Generally, when you think of an exhibition, you think of period pieces or couture pieces. The show is really part of pop culture now!

According to recent reports, MF: I was surprised when fashion magazines [criticized the show] at the beginning. I’m not a fashion designer, [but] I love fashion and I love clothes. This show was not about fashion at the beginning. [Emily] is a bubbly character with a very strong personality from Chicago; she couldn’t have come dressed in Comme des Garçons or in Yamamoto. I needed to have this cultural shock. She’s a fish-out-of-water character, and we needed something to catch the audience’s eyes. When you want to show people that you love the culture but you can’t express it because you don’t know the codes, you don’t speak the language, the only way you find it is through clothes. It was never about “fashion.” Sometimes, it’s about creativity, individuality, making something not trendy at all. The audience got that, and fashion magazines didn’t get it, so they killed me.

Industry observers note that MF: Many times, I’ve asked myself, “Why does this little gingham suit have so much influence?” It’s quite simple. It was the most duplicated, copied, reposted, fan-arted, and used as a Halloween costume. It touched people because it was for them. The French can have their own version of it, their own concept, but for the entire world, it was this one little girly, timeless outfit with the red beret, the red lips, the red soul.

Sources indicate that MF: She read the bad press after the release of season 1, and we had a talk. I mentioned they hated it in France; they find it hideous. [I asked her] “Do you want me to change [it]?” She was smiling and said, “No, we can’t, and we won’t please everybody. We need to keep this strong DNA. We need to continue to have this unexpected silhouette because it’s what catches the audience’s eye.” It’s a guilty pleasure. We can say, I love it.

It opens a way for the audience to see fashion in a different way, where you can mix in an awkward way and free people from this law where you shouldn’t [do that]. Coco Chanel used to say, “Before leaving a room, look at yourself in the mirror and take something out.” I always say, “Put something more on.”.

Sources indicate that MF: I wanted to present a more elevated version, more mature, more evolved, but still true to what she was and what she is, with an eclectic combination and a little bit awkward. She knows the French rules, but as I do, she finds French fashion so boring. In general, I find that fashion is less and less interesting. Why are fashion and celebrity stylists sourcing more and more from archives? What it’s showing is that now everything is the same. Everything is boring, and I understand why. They need to sell the show! We don’t have to sell anything. We have to sell dreams, illusions, craziness, boldness. People watch the show in groups. Some people say, “I love it,” and some say, “I hate it,” and they have a dialogue and fight and have a good [time]. We love that.

MF: A young designer wants to be famous right away. Fame doesn’t happen, and it doesn’t matter. You need to be happy with what you’re doing. With costume design versus fashion design, you can be much freer. You don’t have anything to sell, and you don’t have to design the “It bag.” If your show is successful, it’s a win-win for everybody. To see that, you need to be true to your vision. You need to be true to your gut feeling, to your vision, to your DNA. Talent is not enough; you need to be at the right place at the right time. Being discovered by Darren Star … he changed my life. At some point, you find the right project for you.

You need to work a lot to take care of every detail. You need to be strong and push the boundaries. You need to try to show a different way to see costumes and clothes, to see that everything is possible…. Style begins when fear ends. You don’t want to please everybody, and I’m always attracted to people who dress in a different way, and I’m never judgmental. To create something is to expose yourself. It’s very vulnerable. It’s brave.

This interview has been condensed and edited for clarity.

Pink Hair Is Back and Everyone From SZA to Adéla Are Making a Case for It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (925 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, remember when Kylie Jenner was changing her hair color about every other week, Tumblr was overflowing with pastel-haired girlies, and we were all contemplating whether we could pull off pink hair?
  • Industry observers note that and the range is range-ing.
  • Recent findings suggest that short answer: Yes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, remember when Kylie Jenner was changing her hair color about every other week, Tumblr was overflowing with pastel-haired girlies, and we were all contemplating whether we could pull off pink hair? Well, dust off your 2016 Pinterest boards, bb, because pink hair is officially making a comeback. But this time, it’s not just King Kylie leading the charge. SZA, Adéla, and even Martha Stewart have been putting their own spins on the color, proving that there’s no one way (or age!) to enter your pink hair era. “Since pink is not a natural hair color, you don’t really have to abide by any typical color analysis rules,” says colorist Emily Claire, which means you have free range to do whatever the heck you’d like.

Industry observers note that and the range is range-ing. From electric pink to soft rose gold, I promise there’s a rosy hue for you. Personally, I’m loving this return to hair color that’s just fun—and I’m not the only one. “Recently my clients with pink hair have been requesting baby pink and deep berry pink,” states colorist Cara Craig. Plus, Cosmo called out pink as a top fall hair color trend this year. So, whether you’re ready to go full-on Barbie or want to experiment with a subtle rosy tint, there’s a pink hair idea with your name on it. Ahead, we’re breaking it all down, including how to choose your shade, what to ask for at the salon, and how to keep your pink hair looking fresh.

Recent findings suggest that short answer: Yes. There’s a truly pink hair color for everyone. “I have clients asking for all shades of pink, from blush and rose gold to hot pink to magenta,” claims hairstylist Alyssa Chapa.

Sources indicate that pink is surprisingly so versatile, so there are plenty of ways to make it work for you. “In my opinion, pink is a neutral. I think of fashion colors as cousins to classic shades,” claims Craig. “So if you are a blonde, consider baby pink. If you are a brunette you’ll want to move to darker pinks and fuchsias. If you want to feel like a redhead then wear rose golds and warm pinks.” She also recommends a violet pink if you prefer keeping things cool-toned.

Recent findings suggest that wondering about how your skin tone will look with pink hair? “I’m personally of the opinion that there is no right or wrong shade for your skin tone,” says Chapa, but if it’s really important to you, here are her tips for finding the best hair color for your skin tone. “Start by figuring out your undertones,” she says. “I like using the veins on the inside of the wrist; if you have blue or purple veins then you usually have cool undertones, green veins mean warm undertones, and a mixture of both is a neutral undertone.” Then, it’s pretty easy from there: Match your undertones to the shade of pink, which your colorist will be able to help out with (think baby or icy pink for cool tones, peach or salmon pink for warm tones, that kind of thing).

According to recent reports, first things first: Bring reference photos to your colorist—we’ve handily included some pics throughout this story for ya. After all, Adéla’s vivid pink and Stewart’s subtle rose gold hair require very different approaches, so you’ll want to make sure you’re specific about what shade you’re after.

“For most people, unless you happen to be naturally blonde, the process would involve lightening your hair to the desired level with bleach, then toning it to the desired pink with a direct dye,” notes Claire.

Sources indicate that need some specific pink hair ideas? These are colorist-approved: “One of my favorite ways to wear pink lately is over classic blonde highlights,” claims Craig. “I also love a pink double process (e.g. Adéla).” Double process just means a two-step coloring method—your colorist will first bleach/lighten your hair, then apply the pink color. You can also go with chunky highlights, “especially a halo hairline where the pink frames the face,” adds Chapa. “Mixing chunky pink highlights in with shades of red or brown to create a kind of calico effect is also popular online.”.

Now for the not-so-fun part: Pink hair doesn’t necessarily equal low-maintenance hair. “No matter the tone, you’re going to have to refresh it in four to six weeks if you want it to stay pink,” indicates Chapa. If you want to go as low-maintenance as possible, a softer pink is the way to go, notes Craig.

For a more natural-looking grow-out or to keep your hair color easy, “your alternatives are to choose an already muted color like a dusty rose or mauve and let it fade to blonde or brunette, or to invest in an at-home color depositing treatment to maintain your pink until your next salon visit,” Chapa states.

You can help extend your color by washing less frequently, using color-safe shampoo and conditioner, limiting heat styling, and incorporating a color-depositing mask or at-home hair gloss. “I always recommend my clients use a pink-tinted shampoo or conditioner to keep up with the color between appointments at home,” says Claire.

Catharine Malzahn is a contributing beauty writer at Cosmo. She’s covered all things skincare, makeup, hair, and more, including trending haircuts and hair colors you have to try.

How The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Showcases Effie Trinket’s Fashion Evolution

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, bina Daigeler is the costume designer behind the newly introduced film, and with her team, she oversaw the creation of every single outfit from scratch, with a few helping accessories pulled from vintage specialists.
  • In a recent development, “Working with Glenn Close, she really came to me and stated, ‘I need to find a thread through all the costumes that are made for me, so that I can understand it,’” says Daigeler.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you follow red carpet fashion, these past few weeks, it’s been impossible to ignore Elle Fanning’s method dressing madness as Effie Trinket. From toy ballerina music box headpieces by Robert Wun fit for a fairy tale to makeup compact dresses (and matching headwear) from Givenchy, the fashion story is strong. All roads lead back to her character as young Effie Trinket from The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which is making its theater debut on November 20. Based on Suzanne Collins’s 2025 novel of the same name, it is set 24 years before The Hunger Games and 40 years after The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes. It begins the morning of the 50th Hunger Games, with a 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and Effie Trinket as a young stylist in the Capitol.

According to recent reports, bina Daigeler is the costume designer behind the newly introduced film, and with her team, she oversaw the creation of every single outfit from scratch, with a few helping accessories pulled from vintage specialists. She began with a mood board that focused on the aesthetic differences between the 13 districts while keeping in mind the personalities of the actors. Drusilla Sickle (Glenn Close) had a devoted board full of Alexander McQueen, John Galliano, and Vivienne Westwood, for instance. “It was really like old couture fashion,” Daigeler tells ELLE. “But pieces that, for me, would age very well, you know, that would keep up in time, because I think that is very crucial when you work on such a famous franchise; that you design for the future. That it’s still interesting in 10 years.”.

In a recent development, “Working with Glenn Close, she really came to me and stated, ‘I need to find a thread through all the costumes that are made for me, so that I can understand it,’” says Daigeler. “That was super vital for her.” Daigeler wove everything together with “cool accessories to give her the strength,” and one very special finale look. “She wanted to have a big finale, you know, like a finale where she really feels like ‘I’m the winner. it’s nothing about Haymitch, it's all about me.’” Think: lots of red.

Recent findings suggest that daigeler also referenced Woodstock, Studio 54, the late ’60s and early ’70s. “I tried really to have a strong concept that has to do with the personality of each character,” she states. Unsurprisingly, given Effie Trinket’s predilection for fashion as a stylist, she was a big focus for Daigeler. “For example, young Effie Trinket, how did she become the Effie Trinket that Elizabeth Banks was? Here she is younger, she is fresh, she doesn’t have a lot of money or a fashion background. So it must be something that looked a little bit vintage that could be done at home, a mixture of fabrics, of textures, of color, something very young and fresh and fun.”.

According to recent reports, early on in the film, we see Effie Trinket’s fashion as improvisational. But Daigeler intentionally showcases her ascension from fashion fan to fashion icon throughout the film. Daigeler says that Effie’s outfits all had to have fun elements. “The black kimono with the flowers and patchwork little waistcoat with a flowery blouse and all the color combinations were very strange, but it worked together,” she says. She also mentions her blue denim, Vivienne Westwood-inspired piece with huge sleeves as being the epitome of young Effie Trinket style.

Industry observers note that “The most vital thing was, for Effie, that she looks fun, but also free, because she is in the Capitol, but is still the freest and the most positive and optimistic character,” says Daigeler. “She doesn’t look like damaged and depressed and she had to come in and cheer them up and she definitely came with a solution. Our heroes somehow could trust her and they were so happy to see her. All the other characters from the Capitol, you really don’t know who you can trust.” Therefore, their aesthetic is darker while Effie is lighter and brighter.

Look out for the fashion Easter eggs throughout the film, like Effie Trinket’s butterfly crystal rings, which were just some of the pieces that Daigeler sourced vintage from one of her favorite specialists from around the world. Elsewhere, Haymitch has his own fashion revolution in a quieter way. “The way also how Haymitch wears the clothes and how they were aged and the colors, everything just comes together,” claims Daigeler. “I think the audience will find, or I hope, that they find that there are things that resemble and they recognize it.”.

Likewise for Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin), the longtime Capitol television host, there’s an emphasis on fashionable suits. “It was very, very important that he can move because he is a very physical actor whom moves a lot, so he needed space in his suits,” indicates Daigeler. “Suits also had to give him power.”.

Recent findings suggest that and for Snow (Ralph Fiennes), too, suiting is used to convey power. “He’s very particular about fabrics, about the cut. So I went to a tailor in London, who I have known for many, many years,” she states. “Snow’s suits we developed really like a little bit, World War II military cuts, with a very strong shoulder and a very strong silhouette and these heavy fabrics, and the right colors. But then we gave him the fantasy through hand-embroidered lapels. It had also the hint to his rose that he always wears, and he has somehow always loved flowers.”.

According to recent reports, fashion is both spectacle and a survival tool in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. The odds are forever in fashion’s favor.

#134834. Butternut Pasta With Sausage and Dates

📅 13 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (512 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Epicurious ↗ Open Full Page

Butternut Pasta With Sausage and Dates

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (512 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Squash and sausage are a heroic autumnal pairing, especially in a weeknight-friendly pasta.
  • Rigatoni’s ribbed surface and large holes help chunky squash sauce cling and bites of seared sausage and date wedge—opting for a nutty whole wheat variety will only add to this meal’s autumnal earthiness.
  • More cozy pastas this way: Balsamic Mushroom and Sausage Pasta; Creamy Red Curry Pasta; and Baked Feta Pasta With Green Sauce.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Squash and sausage are a heroic autumnal pairing, especially in a weeknight-friendly pasta. Butternut is the easiest squash to source—not to mention easily found peeled and chopped (a blessing for those with more timid knife skills). But other winter squash like acorn or red kuri can stand in as desired. Whichever squash you select, a sharp, heavy chef’s knife is best for breaking down the chunky veg. But to make your life easier, microwave the squash for 1 to 2 minutes. It will slightly soften, making it simpler—and safer—to slice through.

Rigatoni’s ribbed surface and large holes help chunky squash sauce cling and bites of seared sausage and date wedge—opting for a nutty whole wheat variety will only add to this meal’s autumnal earthiness.

More cozy pastas this way: Balsamic Mushroom and Sausage Pasta; Creamy Red Curry Pasta; and Baked Feta Pasta With Green Sauce.

Industry observers note that cook 1 medium butternut squash (1½–2 lb.), peeled, halved, seeds removed, cut into 1" pieces (about 6 cups), in a large pot of boiling salted water until very tender, 12–14 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer squash to a medium bowl. Reduce heat to low, cover pot, and leave on burner to keep warm.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium Dutch oven over medium-high. Add 1 lb. hot or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and break up into small pieces with a wooden spoon. Cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, about 3 minutes. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until browned all over and just cooked through, 3–4 minutes more. Transfer to a plate with a slotted spoon.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook 3½ oz. Medjool dates (about 6), pitted, sliced lengthwise ¾" thick, in same pan, turning halfway though, until deeply browned, 3–4 minutes. Transfer to plate with sausage; season with salt.

Add remaining 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil to pan. Add 6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and reserved squash. Cook, scraping up browned bits and smashing squash with spoon to break up, until lightly browned and broken up into a chunky paste (pieces do not need to be even), about 5 minutes.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, return cooking liquid in reserved pot to a boil over high heat. Cook 12 oz. short tube pasta (such as rigatoni) until very al dente, about 3 minutes less than package directions (it will finish cooking in sauce). Drain, reserving 3 cups pasta cooking liquid.

It has been revealed that add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid to squash and break up squash with spoon until a saucy consistency. Add pasta, another 1 cup pasta cooking liquid, and reserved sausage and dates. Increase heat to medium-high; cook, adding more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until pasta is al dente and coated in sauce, 2–3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. sherry vinegar or balsamic vinegar. Taste pasta and add more vinegar, salt and/or pepper if needed.

Industry observers note that “It was fun to get to know each other outside of her trying to murder me, me trying not to get murdered. It was nice to take a moment just for us,” Victor, who played as a Faithful while Katie was one of the season’s Traitors, told the outlet.

As for what their first date entailed? Well, there was certainly no discussion about their time on the show, since Victor banned any mention of it. And, honestly, who can blame him? After all, he was onto Katie’s strategy to potentially target him for murder.

Sources indicate that while her crush on Victor helped her game, Katie admitted that she genuinely enjoyed hanging out with him and even grew close to him throughout the season. It has been revealed that the pair remained coy about whether they’ll keep their showmance going offscreen. When asked if they had plans to go on a second date, Victor shared, “Let’s see. Listen, man, it’s gonna... I don’t know. Getting that first one was an uphill battle, but I think there could be.”.

Recent findings suggest that we’re in a great era for affordable fashion-collab watches. Timex is leading the way: its link-ups with Noah, Todd Snyder, and J. Crew are masterclasses in adding personality to classic designs without going OTT. But don’t count Casio out of the race. The Japanese giant has just followed up its 2024 collab with APC. The pair are perfectly matched: Casio watches are known for being beautifully functional and understated—adjectives that fit APC’s spartan aesthetic too.

Recent findings suggest that the first collaboration between the two brands saw them rework the hallowed A1000 digital-display watch. That release stripped back a lot of the original’s markings and added the APC logo on the dial. This time around, it's the AQ-240 getting a makeover. The case is squarer than the rectangular A1000, and while there’s a narrow window for a digital display, the watch maintains the traditional analog format with hands and hour markers. Here, you get the best of both worlds. The watch is sold out on APC's website but still available through Casio, so act fast if you want one. The silver variant is $110, and the gold goes for $135.

In a recent development, what about the APC-ness of it all? That part is the opposite of loud: as with the previous collab, there isn’t much giving away the brand's participation. We’ve got the APC logo on the dial and the buckle, plus the brand’s guitar-and-dagger insignia engraved out of sight on the caseback. Casio already offers the regular A1000 in a bunch of different colorways, but these two new ones are made specifically for the APC collab. The release includes a silver case with a dark-green dial and another in gold on gold. Both of the pieces have a brushed sun-ray effect on the dial. The vibe is refined and stripped back; this is a fashion watch that almost feels anti-fashion.

Maybe the best way to think about it is as the reverse side of the coin to the excellent latest G-Shock 2500 Series. Both come from Casio, and both are minimal and functional. But the G-Shocks are big and bulky, with a design that seems to tip its hat to Patek Philippe’s Nautilus. These new ones are slim and nearly dressy. Put the two new releases together, and you’ve got pretty much all bases covered. And if those aforementioned Timex collabs felt a bit too classicist for you, then the Casio-APC partnership takes things in a more modern direction. Far from just being a cash grab, the “fashion watch” is now one of the best routes into affordable, on-point horology.

  • According to recent reports, in 2026, wearing a tutu is an undeniable endorphin booster.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that distinctly fluffy, feminine, and over-the-top, the tutu has an unrivaled fashion legacy. Is it any wonder that in the past few weeks, celebrities have been joyfully committed to wearing the frilly staple? It may be peak Nutcracker season, but even so, Balletcore will never die. The aesthetic has experienced its original iteration (dating back to the 1800s), its first fashion wave in the ’50s and again in the ’80s, followed by a darker take, a more grounded look, and yet it still persists. At the center of it is the tutu: Nicole Kidman recently wore a Matthieu Blazy Chanel dress with a perfectly layered tutu tulle confection of a skirt that would give Carrie Bradshaw a run for her money. Elsewhere, Rosalía, Tinashe, and Olivia Rodrigo have all recently donned the tutu. The look right now reads as more punky Y2K or ’80s couture.

The spring/summer 2027 runways were littered with echoes of the tutu, too. Both Chanel and Dior showcased voluminous skirts with tutu-like shapes; Dior’s were made of cut fabric petals. Rising label Agro Studio integrated ethereal watercolor tutus into its recent collection. And it’s impossible to forget Cecilie Bahnsen’s undying dedication to the garment. Her fall/winter 2026 collection was a tribute to movement and dance and repositioned the tutu as an everyday item versus occasionwear, pairing it with fleeces and down jackets as live dancers wove throughout the venue wearing tutus. “They brought a beautiful femininity and softness to the more utilitarian pieces, creating an interesting contrast,” Bahnsen tells ELLE. “And as the dancers moved through the show, the tutus came to life, adding a wonderful sense of volume, lightness, and movement to the silhouettes.”.

According to recent reports, in 2026, wearing a tutu is an undeniable endorphin booster. Perhaps it’s deeply and satisfyingly impractical, the exact opposite of wearing a pair of denim jeans and a T-shirt or button-down, the kinds of items that typically dominate capsule wardrobes. “I love the femininity, the sculptural quality, and the beautiful bounce and movement of a tutu,” adds Bahnsen. “There is something so joyful, light, and full of positive energy about it.”.

It has been revealed that given the tutu’s broad history, it’s no wonder vintage tutus are experiencing a bit of a revival too. According to Haile Lidow, founder of Lidow Archive, there’s been a surge in demand. “The tutus I can’t keep in stock right now are lighter and more ballerina-focused,” she tells ELLE. “I have this David Dalrymple for Patricia Field white tutu skirt that was made to be like the famous Carrie Bradshaw title sequence look, and that piece has been renting out constantly. I’ve also been obsessed with tattered tulle lately and the line it tows between innocence and darkness.”.

Sources indicate that like Bahnsen, she sees an inherent joy in the silhouette and also links the current wide appeal to the extra textural feeling. “There’s something very tactile about tutus, and in an age of digital-everything, I think we’re craving pieces that seem to reach out and ask us to interact with them IRL,” she adds. In a season of pared-back dressing, the tutu’s frothy excess feels like a joyful rebellion.

12 Watches That Make a Great Gift for the Man in Your Life

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1294 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s not something casually given—not a tie or a fancy notebook or even a good pen or a nice bottle of booze.
  • According to recent reports, but what watch?
  • The Khaki Field Expedition is the quintessential field watch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A watch is a sentimental gift. It’s not something casually given—not a tie or a fancy notebook or even a good pen or a nice bottle of booze. Don’t get me wrong, those are delightful things to receive and all appropriate for a run-of-the-mill holiday or birthday celebration. But some years aren’t run-of-the-mill. Some years require something extra. Some years are watch years—and trust me, you’ll know it when you get there.

According to recent reports, but what watch? It’s a personal choice, of course, but a personal choice that you’re making for someone else. Luckily, you likely know them pretty well. Around these parts, Esquire knows watches pretty well. Here are 12 suggestions, in price ranges from midwestern frugal to multigeneration inheritance. No matter how much you’re comfortable spending, you can’t go wrong with any of these watches.

A classic watch for a classic guy. The Khaki Field Expedition is the quintessential field watch. Rich history of American craftsmanship, purpose-driven aesthetics, functional compass bezel (even if I can’t figure out how to use it for the life of me), and in the past few years it’s been available with the always practical NATO strap. It’s an ideal watch for the horologist, who’ll appreciate the history, the movement, and the exhibition case back. Win-win, guaranteed all-star gift.

I’m an unabashed Citizen fan. The Promaster “Fugu” is my favorite watch in the $500 range, and the Japanese brand’s Eco-Drive offerings are even more affordable. The Promaster Sea Eco-Drive is almost criminally underpriced for the watch that you get. We’re talking an emerald-green dial with a matching unidirectional 60-minute bezel, 200 meter depth rating, and a stainless-steel bracelet for well under $300. This is a great gift for the practically driven, classic dive-watch fan. And if the green dial is too swerve-y, the black and the blue are both excellent choices.

Recent findings suggest that good doesn’t always mean expensive. A major ol’ dive watch isn’t appropriate for every occasion or every guy. Simpler can be better. Like this under-$100 life-proof G-Shock. It treads the line between classic G-Shock aesthetics and little Casio reference. A watch equally appropriate for a man who never thinks about watches or one who is always thinking about watches—Schrödinger’s timepiece of no taste or good taste. And, hot take, it pairs better with a suit than sneakers do. Keep your shoes formal and let your watch carry the high-low combo.

In a recent development, if he’s not a G-Shock man, he may be an Ironman. A Timex Ironman, that is, even if he’s not logging an insane amount of weekend mileage. As the world grows wary of increased technocracy-driven smart designs, there’s a simple nostalgia to the ’90s-tech runner’s watch. Turns out they were right all along. You don’t need a phone on your wrist, just a stopwatch and an alarm clock and a 100-lap memory to boot. I also like the orange accents here. If he is midwestern frugal and would object to a gift over $100, this scaled-back version also plays.

Shinola’s Duck Watch references ’60s and ’70s skin divers, which sounds dirty but really is just a term for smaller, less depth-rated dive watches and the culture of free diving and spearfishing around them. That’s a reductive explanation that some watch nerds will quibble with, but it’ll serve us for now. The two key things to take away are 1) there was a magazine of the same name that you can find on eBay and 2) Shinola’s modern version is a killer watch. I have this one in Canary Yellow, but I recently borrowed the upcoming Mallard Brown colorway for a photo shoot, and I love it. Hated to send it back. In the sun, the dial turns almost iridescent, like the titular duck’s feathers. It’s battery powered, water-resistant, and not fussy at all.

[Editor’s note: The Mallard Brown colorway is currently out of stock, so for the time being we will direct you to the Canary.].

Let’s get fancy. But let’s get fancy with purpose. More on Rolexes soon, but I think Panerai makes the most exciting watches in the $5,000 to $15,000 range. I realize that’s a large range, one encompassing the price of a decent motorcycle or a used Camry, but I’m talking luxury Swiss-made watches here. This is the tip of the iceberg. Panerai has design panache and exquisite movements, a design that’s not too “look at me” but still far enough outside the classic mold that it demands a second look. It’s not a watch for everyone, but man, those who will love it will love it immensely.

Recently I hosted a friend and fellow style writer for a will-not-be-named rival publication at the Detroit headquarters of T-shirt maker Soft Goods MFG. He had a couple enviable pieces (understated Nitty Gritty corduroy jacket, Paraboot derbies, perfectly faded vintage Levi’s), but I kept looking at his watch, a Unimatic Quattro. In the interest of individuality and my own love of a good suede, I’m suggesting this Todd Snyder collab as the next gift for that extra-special man in your life. It’s Unimatic with a twist, Italian design with an Americana POV, like spaghetti western for your wrist. Clint Eastwood fans rejoice.

It has been revealed that timex and J. Crew’s recent trout-forward collab watch sold out in an instant—unfortunately before I could get my hands on one. But there are other options for the outdoorsy dude. Especially one who cares about stopping forest fires. This Vero Smokey Bear option toes the line between campy and classy with aplomb. It’ll look good while you’re chopping wood or a little Wes Anderson–y at the lodge with a glass of bourbon in hand, telling stories about the trout that got away.

Industry observers note that TAG can get a bad rap in the watch-collecting community, but ignore the critics, especially if your intended recipient is a racing enthusiast. TAG Heuer has a long history in F1 and Grand Prix, and it looks as much at home in the cockpit of a fancy Brad Pitt–piloted car as it does in the fan stands or the sports bar. If you want to step it up a level, the Monaco is a luxury take on a race-day watch—all European angles and rich leather.

Sources indicate that this is the only pilot’s watch on the list—and for good reason. It’s the most handsome pilot’s watch on the market. Marathon developed these in partnership with the Kelly Air Force Base in 1986 and specced it out to withstand high-altitude flight, or even an ejection. If you’re in the market for a classic pilot’s chronograph, Bremont makes the best one. But if you are in the market for a no-frills, all-style, practically designed pilot’s watch, the Marathon Arctic Navigator is your ticket.

Maybe he’s a Rolex Pepsi guy, but you’re on a non-Swiss-made budget. I’ll let you in on a secret: Seiko makes a pretty damn good approximation. I particularly like that this one is PADI co-branded and automatic, with a 200 meter depth rating. Even better, it’s under $500.

For my money, Doxa makes some of the most interesting dive watches out there. Is this on the list because I’d really love if someone took the hint and bought one for me? Hard to say. What’s easy to say is that the orange-dial Doxa Sub 200T is a showstopper. It’s got a slightly smaller profile and a more interesting silhouette than the original 200 but still retains the necessary details, like its unidirectional rotating bezel with its integrated U.S. Navy no-decompression limit table. No rules on whether that’s used underwater or just at the dinner table, either. It’s good to know how long to cook a steak for.

#134825. Creamy Miso Mushroom Pasta

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Epicurious ↗ Open Full Page

Creamy Miso Mushroom Pasta

📅 15 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that mushroom fans: Bookmark this recipe immediately.
  • A few helpful notes for pasta success: (1) While any pasta will work, egg-based noodles, like the fettuccine I recommend here, are the best complement to the sauce.
  • Find more fall favorite meals here: Weeknight Pumpkin Chili; Cream-ish of Mushroom Soup; Mushrooms au Poivre.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that mushroom fans: Bookmark this recipe immediately. It will give you everything you want when you crave a creamy mushroom pasta as soon as the crisp fall air sets in. The hardworking trio of miso, Parmesan, and touch of soy sauce delivers an umami bomb of flavor that doesn’t overwhelm, but magnifies, the best of earthy mushrooms. Coupled with luscious noodles enrobed in a creamy (but not heavy) sauce, what’s not to love?

A few helpful notes for pasta success: (1) While any pasta will work, egg-based noodles, like the fettuccine I recommend here, are the best complement to the sauce. The nests (Rummo and De Cecco are great accessible brands) cook far faster than standard straight pasta, almost as fast as fresh. (2) Don’t be afraid to season your mushrooms! Yes, I know this goes against all that we’ve learned about salting them too early in the cooking process, but just a bit of salt will get them going and releasing their water faster for eventual crisp-browned edges. Don’t be alarmed if you see a pool of water at the start of the mushroom cooking—that’s to be expected and just keep going until it evaporates. (3) Don’t forget to reserve plenty of pasta cooking liquid, which is critical to the eventual sauce’s success. I prefer transferring the al dente noodles from the pasta pot to the skillet, letting any residual water come with it (and to ensure you don’t accidentally drain away that liquid gold).

Find more fall favorite meals here: Weeknight Pumpkin Chili; Cream-ish of Mushroom Soup; Mushrooms au Poivre.

Cook 12 oz. egg-based pasta (such as fettuccine nests) in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 1 minute less than package directions.

Meanwhile, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over high. Add 1 lb. crimini or mixed mushrooms (such as button, maitake, oyster, and/or shiitake), sliced ¼" thick or torn into bite-size pieces, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt and toss to coat evenly. Spread out into an even layer and cook, undisturbed, until mushrooms are starting to release their liquid, 2–3 minutes (do not be alarmed; there will be a lot). Continue to cook, tossing occasionally, until moisture is almost completely evaporated and edges of mushrooms are starting to brown, 6–8 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium-high; add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, tossing often, until garlic is fragrant and golden, 1–2 minutes. Pour in ¾ cup dry white wine, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan with a sturdy spatula or flat-edged wooden spoon, and cook until wine is mostly evaporated (you should have about 1 Tbsp. liquid left in pan), about 4 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 2 Tbsp. white miso and stir until melted and combined. Slowly pour in ½ cup heavy cream, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan; simmer until thickened slightly, 2–3 minutes. Add 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce; season with freshly ground pepper. Taste and add more salt if needed.

Recent findings suggest that using tongs, transfer pasta to mushroom mixture and add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Increase heat to medium and bring to a simmer. Cook, tossing constantly and adding ½–1 cup more pasta cooking liquid to reach desired sauce consistency if needed, until pasta is al dente and liquid has thickened slightly, about 3 minutes.

Industry observers note that remove pan from heat. Add 1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup) to pasta and toss to combine. Season generously with more pepper; taste and season with more salt if needed.

Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan and pepper.

#134821. Are You a Super Ager? This Competition Will Be the Judge of That

Are You a Super Ager? This Competition Will Be the Judge of That

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1358 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alan Krepack stands with his hands on his hips and takes a deep breath as he sizes up the Over Under: an obstacle with a high wooden box and low wooden beam spread 10 meters apart.
  • As soon as the volunteer states “go” he sprints to the box, plants his hands, and hoists his feet up and over.
  • The challenge is just the first of eight trials Krepeck will tackle throughout the day alongside his sons, Harrison and Aaron, at the Super Age Games, a fitness and mental competition designed to assess abilities associated with healthy aging.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alan Krepack stands with his hands on his hips and takes a deep breath as he sizes up the Over Under: an obstacle with a high wooden box and low wooden beam spread 10 meters apart. Music booms over the speakers and other competitors shuffle around the cavernous room of the Armory Track in Washington Heights, New York, but Krepack stays laser-focused, thanks to years of meditation practice.

As soon as the volunteer states “go” he sprints to the box, plants his hands, and hoists his feet up and over. As he lands on the other side, he sprints to the beam, dropping down into an army crawl. “Take your time, take your time,” his son yells from the sidelines. Krepack reaches the far end, rushes back, and repeats the sequence again before crossing the line in 51 seconds. To cool down, he paces back and forth with his hands on his head. “I think I’m a sprinter, I’m a jumper, but then it’s like, fuck, no, I’m 73 years old,” he says, catching his breath.

The challenge is just the first of eight trials Krepeck will tackle throughout the day alongside his sons, Harrison and Aaron, at the Super Age Games, a fitness and mental competition designed to assess abilities associated with healthy aging. On November 7th, the inaugural day-long event drew 530 athletes from 42 states and 15 countries, and about 70% of participants were between the ages of 40 and 64. Krepeck agreed to let me shadow him to understand this newly introduced event through the lens of someone who is, in fact, aging, and would like to do so gracefully.

The name of the Games comes from a buzzword that originated in the longevity world: super ager. The term was originally coined by Northwestern University researchers to describe adults over 80 whose memories rival those of people 30 years younger. These days it’s thrown around on podcasts and in books to describe anyone who defies both the typical trajectory of both cognitive and physical aging.

The inaugural Super Age Games drew 530 athletes from 42 states and 15 countries.

Industry observers note that from crawling across a cargo net to reading microexpressions, the challenges in the competition measure longevity markers like functional strength, aerobic capacity, balance, and cognitive skill. At the end, athletes see where they rank among their age group and receive their “Super Age,” learning how their body’s physical fitness stacks up against the general U.S. population’s.

Industry observers note that in an era where your average middle-aged midwestern dad is training for Hyrox, and a newly introduced, outlandishly extreme challenge is being invented every few months, the Super Age games are a low-key counterpoint to raw, stunty, athleticism, born from the metric-obsessed fitness subcultures who prize longevity above all. And now that fitness trackers like Whoop or Apple Watch can track VO2max, heart rate variability, and resting heart rates, that group continues to grow. Along the way, these stats have become status symbols on par with owning a Lamborghini. And now that overall health is quantifiable, fitness values have become less about just how fast you run or how much you lift, but how slowly aging.

It follows that, despite its name, Super Age Games isn’t just for aging athletes. The crowd there leaned middle-aged, and the youngest person at the competition was 21. As we stood by the dead hang station, Krepak pointed across the room at a brolic young man who looked like he could be an NFL prospect: “That dude’s a serious athlete,” he states, as we watched him run around the track cradling a sandbag on his shoulder.

Sources indicate that unlike competitions like Hyrox, where athletes race through a sequence of workouts against the clock, the Super Age Games allows competitors to rest as long as they need between trials. In fact, Junior Kennedy, the fitness program director for the Games, encourages it. “There's no rush,” he states. “The goal is to get through each event as intentionally as you can. We need to understand what it means to recover.”.

According to recent reports, each trial was developed with a certain longevity marker in mind, and developed with input from researchers at the Buck Institute for Research on Aging, a leading nonprofit research center based in Novato, California dedicated to understanding aging. The Over Under, for example, tests agility by judging how fast you can change levels and switch directions. Meanwhile, the Synapse, a challenge where participants track moving balls on a screen and identify them after they've been shuffled around, is meant to measure cognitive processing.

Challenges in the competition measure longevity markers like functional strength, aerobic capacity, balance, and cognitive skill.

According to recent reports, krepack, a psychologist and lifelong athlete from Mill Valley, California, first heard about the event through its founder, David Stewart. Stewart is a media founder behind two niche longevity platforms, AGEIST and Super Age, where he writes about longevity, wellness, and redefining aging (one of his website testimonial’s says he has made aging “cool and aspirational.”). Krepack’s generally a skeptic of the profit-driven modern wellness industry—“I've always had a jaded view of all of that stuff,” he says—but he has followed both Stewart and the Buck Institutes’ work for years.

The competition appealed to Krepack, in part because he’s spent decades cultivating a consistent exercise routine he’s proud of. He played baseball in college and has spent much of his life skiing, cycling, and playing other sports. These days, his schedule revolves around a handful of rituals: bike rides on Mondays and Fridays, a Saturday hike with a friend, gardening, yoga, and Zen meditation most days. When he signed up for the Games in June, he altered his exercise routine, lifted more weights, practiced hanging from a bar, and experimented with the Neurotracker cognitive test online.

Yet all that training didn’t prepare Krepack for the biggest surprise of his day. After scoring well on both the Inferno (the assault bike VO2max test) and Synapse, next came the fourth trial: the “Tightrope,” a balance challenge that requires competitors to walk along a low beam while carrying a water-filled bag, taking as many consecutive steps as they can in two minutes without falling. He had expected to excel, thanks to years of skiing and yoga. Instead, he struggled to keep steady as the water shifted inside the bag. As his foot slipped off the bar, his eyes got wide. “I can’t believe my balance,” he says. “That’s my one disappointment in life now.”.

Alan Krepack's sons Harrison and Aaron during the “tightrope” challenge.

Krepack was still hard on himself as we walked over to the dead hang trial. But after beating both his sons’ times, he seemed to get his competitive spirit back. He pushed through the remaining challenge determined to finish strong. And he did: By the end of the Games, he had placed second overall, with scores adjusted for age.

A few days after the competition, I checked in with Krepack to ask him how he’d processed the event. He responded with screenshots of his scores. His highest score came from the cargo net, which he credited to sheer determination rather than any particular finesse: “due to my will and overcoming an unconventional and desperate style!” he texted me, “Plus my sons were great support and focus partners.”.

But the Games were also a reality check about aging: “I left there feeling both young and old,” he tells me on a phone call. As he watched his sons rocket through the obstacles, he was forced to confront how much of his athleticism he’d lost. “They just flew over it. They were so fluid, and so fast,” he notes. “I’m not 30 or 40 or 50 or 60 anymore.”.

Despite all the longevity industry's promises of maintaining youth, Krepack sees little value in denying the inevitable. Aging well, he states, is about “accepting, improving, and doing your best. It’s not a denial of who you are at this point in life.” The goal, he says, is to make the most of what you’re still capable of.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I haven’t made a meal in the French countryside in fall; but sometimes I dream, and these slow-cooked lentils are what I’d make in such a situation. Back in my American reality, it still makes an excellent dinner or hearty weekend lunch. Look for mild smoked Austrian or German sausages, which lean on mellow herbs and warm spices (sometimes, if you’re lucky, they’re also stuffed with a nutty cheese)—this style is already cooked to a safe temperature, but the casing’s texture is greatly improved when seared before reheating. If your shop only carries sweet Italian sausage or something like an apple-stuffed chicken sausage, both work in a pinch. What a treat it will be to actually finish off that gallon of apple cider you impulsively bought last week in the lentil-braising liquid.

More great fall recipes this way: Charred Cabbage With Sausages and Apples; Pork Chops With Green Chiles and Apples; Mustardy Cider-Braised Pork Chops.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 6–8 smoked Austrian or German sausages (1–1½ lb.), turning often, until deeply browned on all sides, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Sources indicate that combine 1 large red or yellow onion, finely chopped, 3 celery stalks, finely chopped, 1 large carrot, peeled, finely chopped, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in same pan. Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring often and scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan, until vegetables are softened, 6–8 minutes. Add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and cook, stirring, just until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Industry observers note that add 2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 1½ cups apple cider, 1½ cups French green lentils, picked through, rinsed, ½ cup finely chopped parsley, 3 Tbsp. Dijon or whole grain mustard, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt to pan. Increase heat to high and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid is slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Cover pan, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook until lentils are tender and most of the liquid is absorbed but mixture is still saucy, 30–35 minutes.

In a recent development, uncover pan and stir in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar. Nestle sausages into lentil mixture and add any juices pooled on plate. Simmer until sausages are warmed through, about 5 minutes. Top with parsley leaves and reserved celery leaves to serve.

Industry News: I Am the Wildest Dream of Every Black and Brown Trans Woman Before Me

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that as an influencer, a lot of times I'm the only trans person—or the only trans person of color—in the room.
  • Recent findings suggest that that’s especially true in this current political and cultural climate.
  • It’s been particularly challenging, too, as a trans person in the public eye; there's been many instances where my safety has been jeopardized.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as an influencer, a lot of times I'm the only trans person—or the only trans person of color—in the room. It’s a lot of pressure, and there have been times where I have anxiety before going to certain spaces because I will question "Do I belong here?" But I’ve learned that that’s just the patriarchy and society trying to make us feel like we're not worthy.

Recent findings suggest that that’s especially true in this current political and cultural climate. The trans community, especially the Black and brown trans community, gets so much hate—that’s why I’m very offended when people say being trans “is a choice.” Like, living with and navigating these stigmas and mistreatments isn't something that someone would willing choose.

It’s been particularly challenging, too, as a trans person in the public eye; there's been many instances where my safety has been jeopardized. When I get looked at, I'm thinking, They're looking at me either because I'm pretty or because I'm a viral trans person online. The differentiator is literally if I'm being chased home, which has happened multiple times. Since I speak out for trans women that can't speak for themselves, I'm also putting myself at risk. But at the same time, I think I can also make it safer for the next girl down the line.

It's so rewarding being that person others can look up to. I love reassuring other trans women that they can do certain things or just live their lives authentically, loud, and open. But sometimes I'm like, Oh my god, how nice and easy would it be for me to just be silent and be in the background? But I don't think I was born to be a background girl. I'm front and center.

In a recent development, and I think that the trans women before me would want me to be. The hard work that those women put for girls like me now, I have to show up for that. I think about trans women on the front lines of trans rights, like Marsha P. Johnson or Sylvia Rivera—they were front and center at Stonewall. They were the voices for many then, and there was so much more violence. The community was pretty much hidden at the time, too.

There's so much trans history lost, and Trans Day of Remembrance resurfaces those stories. A lot of times things get pushed under the rug because trans people are seen as not vital to the media, or people in general, especially after all the propaganda that's been pushed out by certain administrations. But every year on this day, I learn about a different girl, especially outside of the U.S. I’ve learned so much about how some surgeries started because certain trans women needed gender-affirming care, and they paved the way for girls down the line.

Education is the number one thing. I want people to know that your understanding of trans identities is not what you think and that there's a lot more to learn. There are times when I get frustrated because I see the stigmas and the rhetoric online that's really just misinformation, rumors, and lies that people make up about trans people. A lot of trans women have died because that ignorance can lead to trans violence. It's really sad to see. But we made it back then—and it was hard then—so we'll make it now. We're a strong community.

Industry observers note that the trans community, we show up for ours (for the most part). There's a couple spaces made for Black trans queer people, like the Black Trans Kitchen by Queen Jean—it’s really beautiful. And Gia Love created the annual Celebration of Black Trans Women Cookout. Trans women that make spaces like that really inspire me because they remind our community that we matter. And we as trans people need spaces where we can just be ourselves, and really show care to one another. Those spaces not only keep me humble, but also remind me of everything I've been through. It makes me feel so grateful and privileged to be alive today because a lot of girls don't make it.

It has been revealed that with the work that I do and everything I create, I want other trans women to see me and know that they belong and that they can be in those spaces too. I want to see more, especially more trans women of color, in positions of power and in rooms where you rarely ever see them.

I hope other trans women see that they can be their most authentic self, and that they can feel confident regardless of what anybody states. If you believe you're an amazing, beautiful person, it will reflect on the outside. I want people to feel that way and do that inner work because it's vital, especially for our survival as trans people.

A Landmark Exhibition Honors Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe’s Yanomami Roots

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it was no small journey for Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe to reach the Institute of Contemporary Art Miami, where a landmark exhibition marks the Venezuelan artist’s first solo museum presentation in the United States.
  • Recent findings suggest that at a preview of the exhibition earlier this week, the soft-spoken Hakihiiwe discussed what he hopes his oeuvre can carry forward.
  • The expansive exhibition, organized by ICA Miami and the Fondation Cartier pour l’art contemporain, brings together more than 100 works across three decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it was no small journey for Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe to reach the Institute of Contemporary Art Miami, where a landmark exhibition marks the Venezuelan artist’s first solo museum presentation in the United States. A member of the Yanomami tribe, Hakihiiwe was raised in the remote Poripori community along the upper Orinoco River, where he still lives. It requires a flight, eight days via boat, and three days via canoe just to reach Caracas, the capital of Venezuela. Getting there takes patience; so does the work, which begins with looking closely at the forest around him.

Recent findings suggest that at a preview of the exhibition earlier this week, the soft-spoken Hakihiiwe discussed what he hopes his oeuvre can carry forward. “My work speaks of my ancestors and I would like it to speak of the future too,” he said in Spanish. “Today our rivers, our lands, what we plant and what we eat are threatened by illegal mining, pollution, and climate change.”.

The expansive exhibition, organized by ICA Miami and the Fondation Cartier pour l’art contemporain, brings together more than 100 works across three decades. (Hakihiiwe’s first solo U.S. survey is also the Fondation Cartier’s first exhibition to open stateside; previous U.S. presentations followed European debuts.) Designed by Mauricio Rocha’s Taller de Arquitectura, the galleries take cues from the traditional Yanomami shapono, or communal house, with dim, filtered light and natural pigments.

The show opens with Hakihiiwe’s early works from the 1990s: delicate drawings on handmade paper that trace animal tracks in the forest, acting as a visual language that continues to shape his practice. Beginning here was intentional, claims Michela Alessandrini, curator at the Fondation Cartier. The early works lay the groundwork for what follows.

Sources indicate that “We wanted to share the evolution of his visual language,” claims Alessandrini, who collaborated with ICA Miami’s curator Gean Moreno for over one year to survey Hakihiiwe’s work for the show. “Across the galleries, you witness his power of observation, from the forms and signs he discovers in the forest to the delicate relationship between all living things that share it.”.

It has been revealed that from there, the installation turns to the Amazonian ecosystem, from studies of individual plants to monumental works shaped by Hakihiiwe’s shamanic practice. In “Puu motho shipe” (Stinging Vines), an acrylic-on-paper work, he records a plant species through winding vines set against a graphic yellow backdrop. Like much of the artist’s practice, it preserves traditional ecological knowledge as the rainforest faces mounting threats. “Ushuemi wake u” (Red Bird Water), meanwhile, comes from a body of work shaped by the artist’s recent shamanic training.

Industry observers note that “It introduced a way of thinking about art, nature, and other ways in the world that continues to guide our mission today,” Alessandrini mentioned of Hakihiiwe’s work, which the Fondation Cartier first showcased in its 2022 exhibition “Les Vivants”. “What has always resonated with us is the perspective his work offers. It advises to look beyond our own familial ways of seeing and to recognize a world in which humans, animals, and plants are all interconnected.”.

Hakihiiwe makes many of his creations in Caracas, where he can work away from Poripori’s humidity and insects. His art may travel, but its focus stays close to home: his community and the land around it. Both anthropological and deeply personal, his pieces offer a view from within a community still fighting to protect its land and way of life.

“We shamans cannot heal the water, the earth, the air,” Hakihiiwe stated to close his remarks. “All the shamans are worried. We know that the time is coming, and that if we don’t change, we will disappear.” He continued, “I hope that through my work people can discover the beauty of the forest, but also its importance and how it can raise awareness about this future we see with such concern.”.

Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe is on view at the ICA Miami from November 19 to March 28, 2027.

The Couple Created a Giant Sunflower Walkway For Their Multicultural Sun Valley Wedding

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
