📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the 1980s, Azzedine Alaïa acquired a title that followed him for the rest of his career: the “King of Cling.” The moniker was a fitting one: the Tunisian couturier was renowned for his sculptural, body-centric designs. He experimented with stretch jersey and “anti-stress” fibers to sculpt the body without restricting movement.

It has been revealed that but the nickname was also limiting, failing to capture the full scope of his work. The first major U.S. retrospective devoted to Alaïa, “Azzedine Alaïa: Sculpting Fashion,” at San Francisco’s Legion of Honor, brings his broader legacy into focus through 80 garments and selections from his personal collection of historic fashion.

“As my research went on, I came to realize how key the U.S. market was in Alaïa’s launch,” Laura L. Camerlengo, co-curator of the exhibit and curator in charge of Costume and Textile Arts at the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, tells ELLE. “By the [brand’s] third season, the U.S. was the second highest market after France, [with interest from] both luxury department stores and small independent retailers.”.

The exhibition took shape after Camerlengo reached out to Olivier Saillard, director of the Fondation Azzedine Alaïa in Paris, who became her co-curator. As visitors enter the Legion of Honor’s Rosekrans Court, they encounter a dress designed for Grace Jones: a spring/summer 1986 haute couture look that Jones modeled on the runway and wore to the 1985 Oscars de la Mode. Part of the opening display, titled “The Women Who Made Alaïa,” it sets the tone for a show that recognizes the muses—both famous and private clients—who wore and supported his work.

Also on view are looks made famous by Rihanna—namely, a sheer red halter gown with a flowing train that she wore to the 2013 Grammys—and Tina Turner, whose silk-organza dress embroidered with gold-tone beads from Alaïa’s spring/summer 1989 concludes the exhibition.

The show then turns to Alaïa’s iconography, as Camerlengo puts it: the bandage dress, his work in denim, and zippered dresses, as well as rare, lesser-seen gems. “I was really keen to have early works on view, particularly the pieces from the 1980s, when he was launching his brand,” the curator says. “These are pieces that would have been shown at Bergdorf Goodman when he had his first fashion show in the United States.”.

The exhibition also places Alaïa’s designs in conversation with the museum’s permanent collection. Belle Epoque-style ensembles from his spring/summer 1992 collection appear among 18th-century European paintings and furnishings, including a Canaletto view of Venice and a sofa commissioned for Marie Antoinette.

Alaïa’s own collection of historic fashion, previously shown in the 2023 Paris exhibition “Azzedine Alaïa, couturier collectionneur,” is represented here, too. The gallery includes pieces by fashion houses he admired, such as Lanvin, Chanel, Balenciaga, and Schiaparelli.

Industry observers note that though Alaïa, who died in 2017 at age 82, is remembered for the body-conscious designs that earned him that “King of Cling” title, he was also a renegade in an industry built around constant production. He highlighted collections only when he felt they were ready—a maverick approach that still resonates today—and had his creations worn by a who’s who of the modeling world, from Naomi Campbell to Gisele Bündchen. Many of his designs were featured in the pages of ELLE over the decades.

“He was someone who pioneered a new way of thinking about fashion,” Camerlengo claims. “He was one of the first to question the fashion system and seasonal calendars and the need for trends. He was focused on meticulous craftsmanship and intentionality in design, a sort of precedent to what we think about today, where we are critical of overproduction and overconsumption in fashion.”.

In a recent development, “Azzedine Alaïa: Sculpting Fashion” is on view at the Legion of Honor Museum from Nov. 21, 2026, to Apr. 11, 2027.

Do You Always Have to Sacrifice Passion for Emotional Intimacy?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (911 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that do you remember the beginning of your relationship with your partner?
  • Recent findings suggest that now, your relationship looks a little different.
  • Industry observers note that we’ve collectively accepted that a long-term relationship somehow means the end of passion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that do you remember the beginning of your relationship with your partner? When you would be turned on by just the thought of your fingers sharing space with theirs? When you’d bust into the apartment movie-style, tossing aside layers of clothes because you just couldn’t wait to get to skin?

Recent findings suggest that now, your relationship looks a little different. There are no mental gymnastics before grabbing your partner’s hand and you don’t mind putting your clothes away nicely before jumping into bed. It’s a comfortable, cozy phase—one that you worked hard and long to get to.

But sometimes, you might wish you could have both.

Industry observers note that we’ve collectively accepted that a long-term relationship somehow means the end of passion. You spend months or even years learning everything you can about your partner. You’ve gained trust, a strong foundation, and yet, the passion seems to have disappeared with the uncertainty.

Sources indicate that “The comfort you worked so hard to build may be what’s subtly killing your desire for your partner,” certified sex therapist Dr. Mindy DeSeta, PhD tells Cosmopolitan.

Industry observers note that she explains that over time, we unknowingly become complacent about romancing our partner. All of the exciting unknowns of the beginning of a relationship (Do they want to kiss you? Do they want to come home with you?) eventually fade away.

“You may be intimately familiar with your partner's moves after a number of years, and that's a beautiful thing,” Dr. DeSeta says. “But repetition can dull the excitement of physical intimacy.”.

But contrary to what we’ve all learned to accept, this isn’t an inevitable diagnosis for your long-term relationship. It is possible to have both emotional intimacy and sexual passion. You just have to work for it.

Industry observers note that “Your sex life will suffer if you do not actively continue to learn your partner’s desires,” Dr. DeSeta says.

Recent findings suggest that you might think that you know everything there is to know already about your partner. But as we get older, our desires change—even if our partner doesn’t.

Industry observers note that “Your pleasure is constantly evolving and if you want to continue to have a thriving and exciting sex life, a couple must be able to talk about most recent desires,” she says. “What turned you on at 25 may not still turn you on at 40.”.

This is why communicating your desires and feelings to your partner is so notable. Sure, you and your partner may be pros at working through disagreements and emotionally supporting each other through life’s changes—but does that energy translate into your sex life? Do you share your curiosities? Do you hold space for them telling you they’d like to try something different? If you don’t, it might be time to make a change.

First, in order to feel sexy with your partner, you need to feel sexy yourself. Do something every day that makes you feel sexy and confident,” Dr. DeSeta indicates. “The foundation of a great sex life starts with each person having a thriving libido.”.

Then try to initiate sexy conversation with your partner. Dr. DeSeta suggests planning something that feels tantalizing without the expectation of physical intimacy to follow. Reach each other erotica, talk about new fantasies you’ve had, discuss a trendy sex topic in media.

In a recent development, “Many long-term couples need a prompt to get the sexy conversations started,” she notes. They also need reminders to touch each other more.

“Long term couples are notorious for forgetting physical affection,” she says. Dr. DeSeta emphasizes small touches every day. This can look like caressing their back as you pass them in the kitchen or holding hands while you watch your favorite show on the couch. Instead of maneuvering around each other, lean into the touch. It signals to your partner that you see them and want them throughout the day. And just the feeling of being wanted can ignite some of that passion from the early days of your relationship.

Industry observers note that most importantly, you should date your partner every day. Dr. DeSeta recommends “Daily Dates” to couples she sees in therapy. This is when you set aside 20 minutes everyday to make your partner a priority.

Sources indicate that “All too often long-term couples put their relationship second, so this tune up is always needed,” she says. “During these 20 minutes the phones are silenced, logistical conversations are off the table, and the time is dedicated to emotionally connecting with their partner.”.

Sources indicate that by doing this, she explains that you slow down the daily hustle and really learn how to reconnect with your partner. You might even learn a few fresh things about them in the process.

“If we do not make the intentional effort to keep the passion alive, then you are at risk of falling into autopilot,” Dr.Deseta says. We often think passion and emotional intimacy are at odds with each other, but that’s because we think it’s acceptable to simply fall into our relationship without making an active effort to keep our relationship exciting. And no, you don’t have to be constantly ripping each other’s clothes off or feel nervous in order to have a passionate relationship. But you should aim to feel the same deep desire and attraction to your partner that you did when you first started off—if not more.

Muñoz III, American activist and founder and CEO of Cultural Productions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In Upcoming York City, a lunch reservation at The Plaza is always a good idea. But on Thursday afternoon, there was a particularly good reason to be there. Around 400 guests from the fashion, business, entertainment, and philanthropy worlds arrived at the storied hotel for Citymeals on Wheels’ 39th annual Power Lunch, raising more than $1.3 million to help feed older New Yorkers.

It has been revealed that this year’s honorees included Latest York City police commissioner Jessica Tisch, Imaginary Ventures co-founder Dame Natalie Massenet, and Today co-host Al Roker, each honored for their longtime support of Citymeals. Deborah Roberts, a Citymeals board member and ABC News correspondent, served as emcee.

It has been revealed that A number of familiar faces from the city’s social scene turned out, including Karlie Kloss, Lauren Santo Domingo, Tamara Mellon, and Derek Blasberg. Event chairs Blasberg, Dr. Samantha Boardman, Margo M. Nederlander, and Lizzie Tisch helped bring the afternoon together, alongside Citymeals board co-presidents Anne Cohen and Julie Daum.

It has been revealed that of course, the most notable number of the afternoon wasn’t the guest count. The funds raised will provide approximately 130,000 meals to older residents across the five boroughs, where Citymeals at the moment serves 22,000 people.

For Citymeals CEO Beth Shapiro, the afternoon was a reminder of what a gathering like this can accomplish. “The generosity we saw in the room today is a powerful reminder of what’s possible when New Yorkers come together to care for one another,” she mentioned in a statement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Safe Word is a series highlighting the latest trends in the jewelry market, keeping you up to date on all things that sparkle and shine.

According to recent reports, november’s jewelry debuts are looking both backward and forward, with designers revisiting their roots, reworking archival ideas, and stepping into entirely upcoming territory. First up, Quentin Jones is taking her surrealist art off the wall and onto the body with “Nocturne,” her first jewelry collection; Pomellato reaches back to 1997 to revive “Moneta Orientale” as a colorful modern talisman; David Yurman celebrates the magic of a New York holiday with Michael B. Jordan, Yerin Ha, and Inde Navarrette; Vhernier revisits its iconic “Trottola” design with new proportions and contrasting materials; Di Volpe reinterprets the classic tennis bracelet with customizable gemstones in “DiSegno”; Brent Neale transforms the classic bow into sculptural fine jewelry with “Wrap It Up”; and Kendra Scott launches the new “Kendra Scott Collection,” reimagining her signature Spike motif as a personal talisman. From archival revivals and meaningful motifs to innovative designs and new creative directions, November’s launches prove that sometimes the best way forward starts with looking back. For the rest of the month, we’ve got you covered on all the jewelry-related happenings worth knowing about.

Quentin Jones Turns Her Art Into Jewelry.

Recent findings suggest that quentin Jones is taking her art off the wall and onto the body with “Nocturne,” the first jewelry collection from House of Quentin Jones. Following the multidisciplinary artist’s debut of surrealist ceramics and tapestries last year, the fresh collection transforms recurring gestures and symbols from her work into sculptural collars, cuffs, armbands, pendants, chains, and earrings. Eyes, hands, stars, moons, tears, and knots take shape in silver and gold vermeil alongside freshwater pearls, onyx, opals, jade, glass, and silk tassels, giving the pieces a dreamlike, talismanic quality. Beginning as drawings and hand collages in Jones’s Brooklyn studio, each design carries her surrealist visual language into wearable form, further blurring the line between art, design, and fashion.

Piotrek Panszczyk Makes His Debut at Ippolita.

In a recent development, ippolita is entering a new chapter under creative director Piotrek Panszczyk, who makes his debut at the house with “Ancient Bohemia,” a collection inspired by its archives and the organic forms of nature. Taking a sculptural approach to jewelry, Panszczyk reimagines familiar signatures with an emphasis on texture, craftsmanship, and unconventional layering. The house’s iconic Wavy Disk becomes the Wavy Coin, featuring Hippolyta, Queen of the Amazons and the brand’s namesake, as a symbol of feminine strength. Elsewhere, hand-sculpted Stardust pavé is set entirely with diamonds, pearls make their first appearance, and lightweight, hand-hammered silver Roma links offer multiple ways to wear, from necklaces to belts. Lapis lazuli, mother-of-pearl, and quartz introduce color through Ippolita’s signature layered doublets and triplets, mixed rather than matched for an eclectic finish. The result is a fresh interpretation of the house’s heritage that feels both ancient and distinctly modern.

Jade Trau and Luis Morais Combine Gemstones and Diamonds.

Industry observers note that jade Trau and Luis Morais are joining forces for a limited-edition collection that brings together their different approaches to fine jewelry. Comprised of 16 one-of-a-kind pieces, including 12 bracelets and four necklaces, the collaboration pairs Morais’s colorful gemstone beads with Trau’s signature 18-karat gold and diamond elements. The designs feature a vibrant mix of stones, from chrysoprase and amazonite to lapis lazuli, turquoise, carnelian, and tiger’s-eye, accented by recognizable Jade Trau details like the Frankie rondelle, Sophisticate station, and Georgie diamond lock. Designed with everyday wear in mind, the bracelets lend themselves to layering, while the necklaces incorporate Trau’s diamond-set closures. The result is a playful meeting of color and craftsmanship that brings a fresh perspective to both designers’ signatures.

Lagos Looks to the Stars With Its Latest Collection.

Lagos references the night sky in its latest fine jewelry collection, taking inspiration from the North Star and its centuries-old symbolism of guidance and possibility. Designed to celebrate milestones, new beginnings, and meaningful connections, the “North Star” collection features sculptural star motifs crafted in 18-karat gold and illuminated by natural diamonds. Cascading silhouettes and light-catching details bring a sense of movement to the celestial designs, balancing statement-making shapes with delicate craftsmanship. Both symbolic and sophisticated, the assortment offers a modern interpretation of a timeless emblem, making each piece a reminder of the people and moments that guide us.

Kendra Scott Rolls out an Eponymous Collection.

Kendra Scott is offering a more personal look into her design world with the launch of the “Kendra Scott Collection,” a upcoming line spanning fashion and fine jewelry. Its first edition, “The Spike,” revisits a silhouette the designer has worn throughout her career as a personal symbol of strength, confidence, and conviction. Inspired by nature and the radiance of the night sky, the collection translates the pointed motif into sculptural necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and charms, balancing bold proportions with intricate craftsmanship. Fashion jewelry incorporates tiger’s eye, malachite, and turquoise, while fine jewelry introduces lab-grown diamonds, pavé detailing, labradorite, and lapis. From statement-making links to delicate diamond charms, the collection offers a new interpretation of Scott’s longtime signature, inviting wearers to make the symbol their own.

Alison Lou’s ‘Latest Wave’ Collection Experiments With New Materials.

Recent findings suggest that alison Lou is entering a latest chapter with “New Wave,” a fine jewelry collection that introduces unexpected materials and a fresh approach to the designer’s signature playful aesthetic. Exploring the relationship between movement and form, the collection pairs lightweight titanium and ceramic with lab-grown diamonds, creating fluid, sculptural silhouettes that curve and catch the light. Available in Fig and Denim Blue colorways, the designs include wavy rings, diamond-accented signets, delicate thread necklaces, and statement drop earrings. With its unconventional materials and easy-to-wear designs, “New Wave” brings a new sense of movement to Alison Lou’s everyday jewelry.

Jenny Bird and Emese Gormley Partner on the Anyu Ring.

Industry observers note that jenny Bird is expanding her JB FINE collection with a new collaboration featuring lifestyle creator and Lipstick on the Rim podcast host Emese Gormley. Named in honor of Gormley’s mother, the Anyu Ring offers a personal take on the classic signet, featuring three lab-grown baguette diamonds set in 14-karat yellow or white gold. The understated design combines the timeless appeal of a signet ring with a sentimental tribute to family, bringing a new perspective to Bird’s growing fine jewelry offering. Available exclusively on Jenny Bird’s website, the collaboration makes a case for jewelry that feels as meaningful as it looks.

Pomellato Revives Its 1997 Moneta Orientale Pendant as a Colorful Talisman.

It has been revealed that pomellato is looking to its archives for its latest good-luck charm. For the newest chapter of “Memorie d’Archivio,” the maison revives Moneta Orientale, a 1997 pendant inspired by the ancient symbolism of a circle surrounding a square, representing the harmony between heaven and earth. Made in 33 stone-and-pavé combinations, the design pairs colorful hard stones including black jade, amazonite, sodalite, rhodochrosite, and labradorite with Pomellato’s signature irregular pavé of diamonds, sapphires, rubies, and more. Offered in two proportions, each pendant transforms the archival motif into a modern talisman for prosperity and protection.

Bibi van der Velden Makes Her High Jewelry Debut With ‘Eclipse’.

Sources indicate that bibi van der Velden is entering a new era with “Eclipse,” the designer’s first high jewelry collection and most refined exploration of diamonds to date. Inspired by the fleeting moment when light gives way to darkness, the collection includes two six-piece suites: one in white diamonds and another defined by an ombré of diamonds into gray spinels deepening into black. Van der Velden’s signature alligator motif is abstracted into fluid, sculptural silhouettes, with scales engraved into the white gold on the reverse of each piece. “With Eclipse, I wanted to take those familiar elements and transform them into something more abstract and sculptural,” she states. “It’s a collection about transformation, which has always been at the heart of my work.”.

Aflalo and Leandra Medine Cohen Turn Everyday Indulgences Into Fine Jewelry.

Aflalo is finding the humor in our obsession with wellness with “The Vanities,” a new two-piece fine jewelry capsule designed exclusively by Leandra Medine Cohen. Playing with the contradiction between longevity and life’s little indulgences, the collection transforms two unlikely everyday accessories into precious objects. The Memento Mori is a 14-karat yellow gold cigar band set with more than four carats of diamonds, designed to slip over an Oura Ring, while The Libertine is a sterling silver pendant case adorned with diamonds and a wild-haired woman outlined in gold, designed to hold nicotine pouches or other small essentials. Equal parts extravagant and irreverent, the collection makes a playful case for enjoying life’s pleasures without sacrificing personal style.

Julia Berolzheimer’s Hart Jewelry Collection Draws on Childhood Memories.

It has been revealed that hart is teaming up with Julia Berolzheimer for a new jewelry collection that celebrates the art of the stack. Inspired by Berolzheimer’s childhood memories of her grandmother’s California ranch and her collection of Art Deco minaudières, the collaboration brings together whimsical charms, colorful gemstones, and meaningful talismans designed to be mixed, layered, and restyled. Botanical motifs take shape in Tree of Life coins, daisies, bees, and fruit-inspired charms, while carnelian, turquoise, and pink opal add playful pops of color. One standout is the Perfume Vesta Case, a modern interpretation of a Victorian-era accessory that can hold a sample-sized fragrance and hang alongside other charms. With interchangeable chains, cords, and pendants, the collection makes a case for jewelry that feels just as personal as the memories behind it.

David Yurman Captures the Magic of a Latest York Holiday.

In a recent development, david Yurman is celebrating the magic of the holidays in New York City with a new campaign featuring global brand ambassador Michael B. Jordan alongside actresses Yerin Ha and Inde Navarrette. Set against a snow-covered Washington Square Park, the campaign captures a series of quintessential New York moments, from Jordan and Ha facing off in a spirited card game to Navarrette hailing a cab in search of the perfect holiday gift. Throughout the campaign, the cast wears some of the house’s most recognizable designs, including 18-karat gold Cable bracelets and pieces from the “Starburst” and “Armory” collections. Directed by Bradford Young and photographed by Drew Vickers, the campaign brings together the spirit of the city, the joy of togetherness, and the timeless appeal of David Yurman’s jewelry.

Vhernier Reintroduces Its Iconic ‘Trottola’ Design With New Proportions.

Vhernier is revisiting one of its most recognizable designs with a newly introduced interpretation of “Trottola,” the sculptural collection originally introduced in 2003. Inspired by the continuous motion of a spinning top, the latest designs play with proportions, contrasting materials, and asymmetrical shapes across rings, bracelets, necklaces, and earrings. Polished rose gold meets glossy black jet, with select pieces featuring diamond pavé for an added contrast of light and dark. The collection also focuses on versatility, from rings designed for stacking to convertible earclips that can be worn as studs or dangling earrings. With its fluid forms and unexpected material combinations, “Trottola” brings a fresh perspective to Vhernier’s signature sculptural approach to jewelry.

Di Volpe Reinvents the Tennis Bracelet.

It has been revealed that di Volpe is rethinking the classic tennis bracelet with “DiSegno,” a new customizable fine jewelry system designed to change with its wearer. Using concealed, patent-pending connections, individual cultured diamonds and gemstones, called Elements, can be removed, rearranged, or added by hand, allowing wearers to transform bracelets into necklaces or earrings without compromising the seamless look of traditional tennis jewelry. The collection debuts with 28 stone-and-cut combinations, including rubies, emeralds, sapphires, and diamonds, alongside a limited-edition collaboration with Lebanese artist Ali Cha’aban featuring five sculptural designs. With new cuts, colors, and artist collaborations planned for future releases, “DiSegno” makes the case for fine jewelry that’s never quite finished.

Brent Neale Riffs on the Bow in Fine Jewelry.

Recent findings suggest that brent Neale is putting a bow on the holiday season with “Wrap It Up,” a new fine jewelry collection that transforms the familiar ribbon motif into sculptural works of art. Drawing inspiration from Old Hollywood glamour and the femininity of the 1960s, the designer plays with the contrast between rigid precious metals and the soft movement of fabric, crafting bows that twist, curl, and unfurl in 18-karat gold and platinum. Colored gemstones sit nestled within the ribbon-like forms, while pavé diamonds accentuate every curve and fold. Equal parts playful and precious, the collection brings a little gift-wrapped glamour to the jewelry box.

Grace Winfrey’s ‘Poppy Fortuna’ Collection Reimagines Good-Luck Charms.

Grace Winfrey is bringing a little extra luck to the jewelry box with “Poppy Fortuna,” a latest fine jewelry collection inspired by the natural beauty of the Italian landscape and symbols of good fortune. Scarlet poppies, sunflowers, bees, four-leaf clovers, horseshoes, and ladybugs come to life through vibrant gemstones and intricate pavé, creating miniature mosaics of color and texture. Highlights include a Lucky Bangle combining three good-luck charms, sculptural sunflower earrings with tiny ladybugs tucked into their petals, and layered charm necklaces designed to feel like modern keepsakes. Handcrafted in New York City, each piece transforms familiar symbols of prosperity, protection, and happiness into playful, colorful works of art.

Robinson Pelham Channels ’90s Glamour for Its Anniversary.

In a recent development, robinson Pelham is closing out its 30th anniversary celebrations with “Suite 96,” a new campaign and collection launch inspired by the glamour of late-’90s London. Set inside a private suite at St. James’s Hotel & Club in Mayfair, the campaign considers jewelry the ultimate room service, with diamonds arriving on trays, gold spilling out of wardrobes, and plenty of pieces to layer before a night out. At the center is “Studio 30,” a four-piece anniversary collection featuring diamond necklaces and statement earrings, including the sculptural Via and Hira necklaces, cascading diamond drops, and the bold Solstice Supreme. Alongside the anniversary designs, the house introduces new collections and additions to existing favorites, from chunky gold links and graphic heart rings to colorful enamel and gemstone combinations. Together, the introduces celebrate three decades of Robinson Pelham’s bold, playful approach to fine jewelry.

Le Vian and Jared Revive Georgian-Era Romance.

Le Vian is bringing a little old-world romance to Jared Jewelers with its latest exclusive “Georgian Chocolate & Nude Diamonds” collection. Inspired by the candlelit jewels of the Georgian era, when jewelry was designed to capture and reflect the warmth of natural light, the collection rethinks historic buttercup settings in polished Honey Gold, with eight rounded prongs framing each natural diamond. The designs pair Le Vian’s signature Chocolate and Nude Diamonds with warm gold detailing across solitaire rings, anniversary bands, tennis bracelets, necklaces, and earrings. Select styles introduce colorful gemstones including Chocolate Quartz, Green Apple Peridot, and Grape Amethyst, giving the vintage-inspired silhouettes a contemporary upgrade. With its sculptural settings and warm-toned stones, the collection brings the romance of antique jewelry into the present.

Wempe’s ‘Au:thentic’ Celebrates the Art of Goldsmithing.

In a recent development, wempe’s newly introduced gender-inclusive fine jewelry collection, “Au:thentic,” puts craftsmanship front and center, finding inspiration in the foundational skills taught to aspiring goldsmiths. The collection takes its shape from the jump ring, one of the first techniques Patrick Sieroslawski learned as an apprentice more than 22 years ago, translating its form to necklaces, bracelets, rings, earrings, and pendants. Handcrafted at Wempe’s atelier in Germany, the pieces come in 18-karat yellow, white, and rose gold, with select styles set with diamonds. “Au:thentic” also marks the beginning of a multiyear rollout, with three additional chapters set to expand on its design language through twists, wraps, and interlocking links.

Recent findings suggest that charles Melton has long loved massive, baggy pants. Back in 2024, the actor landed on GQ’s annual list of best pants thanks to one extremely voluminous pair from the Japanese label Sillage. And if his fits this fall are any indication, Melton won’t be stepping away from the assertively wide bottoms anytime soon. In fact, he keeps wearing one fantastically huge pair after another.

Recent findings suggest that the Her Private Hell star’s latest giant-trouser run kicked off in mid-October at the star-studded Academy Gala in Los Angeles. While A-list dressers like A$AP Rocky and Jacob Elordi revealed up in respectfully roomy pants, Melton upped the ante in an ERL tuxedo that left no doubt about his dedication to the slouch. His cropped-front tailcoat was neat as a pin and fit like a glove, but his slacks were dramatically roomy and artfully rumpled—parachute pants gone black tie.

Later that same month, he popped up in Texas for the F1 Grand Prix in a very Fashion Dude outfit: Louis Vuitton workwear jacket, sporty sunglasses, bucket hat, and some choice Wales Bonner x Adidas Sambas. And on his legs? A twisted-seam silhouette billowy enough to make a scrum of downtown stylists and creative directors blush. ​.

According to recent reports, but Melton saved his biggest look of all for last week in Latest York. At a VIP dinner for the South Korean eyewear label Gentle Monster, he donned a matching set from Viviano, the Tokyo-based label from designer Viviano Sue. Cut from gabardine as dark as a moonless night, both his Harrington jacket and balloon trousers looked as though they’d been blown up to the size of a weather balloon and then deflated, leaving behind all the crinkles and creases. He contrasted the dramatic ensemble with a pair of tiny oval sunglasses, which capped the whole thing off just right.

Recent findings suggest that even as menswear’s ideal pant fit moves towards a relaxed straight leg, some guys who dove deep into the baggy waters aren’t quite ready to give their roomy fits up just yet. Melton clearly loves the look and wears it well. And when your gigantic trousers help you stand out in a crowd as effortlessly and stylishly as his do, why bother changing?

Sources indicate that kim Kardashian has finally got the Ferrari red memo. After a pastel pink in the paddock at last month’s Singapore Grand Prix, the Skims founder has gone full-throttle on boyfriend Lewis Hamilton’s team colors. At the Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying session on Friday night, Kardashian turned out to support Hamilton in a look that was full-throttle Ferrari; of course, with a Kim Kardashian twist.

In a recent development, staying true to her second-skin silhouettes, Kardashian wore red leather lace-up leggings with a matching, skintight zip-up top and strappy scarlet stilettos. A black leather trench coat, cinched tightly at the waist, brought it all together, and she added some oversized shield sunglasses and long, glossy black hair to complete the look. Ferrari pit crew, but make it fashion.

Recent findings suggest that kardashian watched qualifying from the Ferrari garage, where fellow guests included George Lucas and Mellody Hobson. With Hamilton behind the wheel, she was making her third Grand Prix appearance of the season—and continuing to establish what’s become a quite fabulous Formula 1 wardrobe in the process.

Recent findings suggest that at the Monaco Grand Prix in June, Kardashian made her paddock debut in a sheer black Gucci bodysuit, flared jeans, pointed stilettos, and those now-familiar shield sunglasses, channeling the original noughties WAGs. For race day, she switched into a draped, one-shouldered cream gown with an open back.

Kim in Singapore wearing Roberto Cavalli spring 2003 collection.

Kim in Singapore wearing Alaïa spring 2024.

Recent findings suggest that then came Singapore, where she eschewed Ferrari red for a sugary sweet pink, wearing a sheer Alaïa spring 2024 turtleneck dress with a matching Hermès Mini Kelly. The following day, she dipped into the Roberto Cavalli archives for a spring 2003 silk chiffon skirt set featuring a corseted waist and floral print.

According to recent reports, through it all, Kardashian has stuck to the style signatures that have long defined her wardrobe: sculpted shapes and statement-making accessories at the center of every look. Seeing her finally commit to her boyfriend's team colors—and while Hamilton may have been eliminated at the Vegas qualifier—the pair are feeling more and more like endgame.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Seasonal travel is exciting, but getting everyone from point A to point B can be a production—especially when babies and pets are involved. Between navigating crowded airports, packing the car with what feels like half your house, and keeping your four-legged family members calm amid all the chaos, there’s a ton to think about. And while you can’t control flight delays, holiday traffic, or the timing of a much-needed diaper change, having the right travel gear can make a world of difference.

In a recent development, enter Nuna and Tavo, two brands that bring thoughtful design, innovative safety features, and a beautiful aesthetic to (often hectic) family travel. Nuna’s premium baby gear helps take some of the stress out of everything from airport security to car-seat installations, while Tavo focuses the same level of attention on the safety and comfort of travel essentials designed specifically for pets. Think lightweight strollers that fold with one hand (because your other one is probably occupied), car seats that don’t require an online tutorial to install, and comfortable carriers that give your furry companions a safe spot of their own.

Whether you’re flying across the country to visit the grandparents, packing up for a holiday road trip, or exploring a latest destination together, these six Nuna and Tavo essentials, available at Bloomingdale’s, can help make the journey a little more joyful for everyone involved.

Sources indicate that given crowded security lines, blowouts at the worst possible moment, and the sheer amount of stuff you have to tote, a lightweight stroller is a genuine lifesaver at the airport. At just 16.3 pounds, the Nuna VIAA cabn is designed to meet IATA cabin-size standards when folded with the armbar removed—though you’ll still want to double-check your airline’s requirements. One-handed steering makes navigating crowded terminals easier (especially when you’re juggling a much-needed iced coffee), while a roomy storage basket holds up to 22 pounds of diaper bags, coats, backup outfits, bottles, snacks, and approximately 47 things to keep your baby entertained. It even comes with a carrier bag for when it’s time to board.

In a recent development, this Nuna duo pairs the TRIV lx stroller, which folds with one hand and stands on its own, with the ultralight PIPA urbn infant car seat. And if you’ve ever broken a sweat or found yourself YouTubing car seat installation instructions for the 100th time, you’ll appreciate that this one clicks into place without a base, using its built-in pipaFIX rigid latch installation. Large rear wheels and all-wheel suspension pair with a spacious storage basket and handy tracking-device pocket to make the stroller ready for everyday outings.

The Nuna SWIV’s standout feature is button-activated 360-degree rotation on all four wheels, allowing it to move sideways and pivot through tight spaces without the struggle of squeezing through crowded airport lines and store aisles that clearly weren’t designed with strollers in mind. A one-handed recline with three positions, including a near-flat option, makes adjustments easy, and the stroller is travel-system-ready with any Nuna PIPA series infant car seat, allowing you to move baby from the car to the stroller.

The Tavo Crispin gives your pet a roomy, comfortable spot of their own, with mesh panels for ventilation and visibility so they can still keep eyes on their humans. It’s impact-tested and secures to your vehicle using lower anchors and a top tether, with a protective memory-foam guard for added peace of mind. And when the holiday travels are over, it collapses for easy storage without taking up precious space at home.

This Tavo travel system might be your new favorite on-the-road companion. The Maeve car seat attaches to the Roscoe Trek stroller frame, so you can go from the car to a festive outing without having to transfer your pup to a different carrier. All-terrain rear wheels and suspension make bumpy sidewalks easier to navigate, while one-touch brakes and a compact stroller fold come in handy when it’s time for a coffee stop or to load everything back into the car.

There’s a very particular type of heart-rate spike that comes with flying with a pet. You have to stand in the airline’s special-assistance line with your (probably nervous) dog or cat, only to finally reach the counter and hold your breath as the agent (and sometimes a supervisor) decides whether their carrier fulfills the rules. The Tavo Dupree II has a chic carry-on design that’s also crash-tested, complete with built-in vehicle connectors and a protective memory-foam guard. Mesh panels keep air circulating, while a trolley sleeve lets you slip it over your suitcase handle instead of carrying everything separately. You’ll still want to double-check your airline’s requirements before flying.

According to recent reports, welcome back to Beauty Marks: Vogue’s weekly edition of the best moments in celebrity beauty, from Vogue editors’ IG feeds, and all the glam of the fashion and pop culture landscapes. Each week, we curate the nail art to pin for your next nail appointment, new recruits to ‘Team Bob’, and major red carpet moments from the week’s most glamorous affairs. As always, it’s as much about celebrity beauty as it is about the makeup artists, hairstylists, and nail artists, as well as the creators crafting the trends you’re about to see everywhere.

According to recent reports, this week, beauty was all about the finer details. Sadie Soverall and Lola Petticrew adopted some statement bangs, while Jessie Buckley, Emilia Clarke, and Jessica Chastain offered three very different takes on the bob. Elsewhere, Simone Ashley and Eva Victor favored sleek, glossy lengths, Jennifer Lopez made the humble nude manicure feel fresh again, and Hailey Bieber delivered a masterclass in winter-ready glam. From Old Hollywood drama to playful, graphic flourishes, there was plenty to bookmark.

Scroll through the week’s best of celebrity beauty and pop culture’s glam below, and head to the app to vote for your favorite.

A little soft glamour goes a long way. For the Governors Awards, Eva Victor chose long, glassy, center-parted brunette hair, paired with subtly smoky taupe eyes, delicately flushed cheeks, and a rosy lip. A balance of warmth and sharp definition. Hair by Justine Marjan, makeup by Yukari.

Jessie Buckley is a brunette once more, opting for a wintry, chocolate shade. At the Ivors Composer Awards, hairstylist Fabio Petri gave her chin-length cut a severe side part and sleek, tucked-under ends. Fresh peachy cheeks and a softly defined nude lip, courtesy of Naoko Scintu, offered a lovely counterpoint.

Winter beauty inspiration, courtesy of Hailey Bieber. A slicked-back bun, softly bronzed cheeks, fluttery lashes, and her signature glossy nude lip make an excellent match for that enormous, fluffy white collar. Makeup by Leah Darcy.

Lola Petticrew’s jet-black lengths and perfectly straight baby bangs, exaggerated, graphic winged eyeliner, and mauve-toned shadow lands somewhere between gothic heroine and sixties doll. Hair by Sami Knight, makeup by Nhinako.

Ella Rubin is captivating with a softly smudged eye and a great nude lip. Makeup artist Shayna Gold created this pretty, gently defined Chanel Beauty look using Les Beiges eyeshadow, Le Liner de Chanel in 512 Noir, and Rouge Coco lipstick in 124 Marie, paired with subtly flushed cheeks and luminous skin.

Trust Jennifer Lopez to make a classic nude manicure feel ultra luxurious. For the premiere of The JLo Show, manicurist Tom Bachik created a juicy peachy nude using shade FS-106 from his NEUDES collection. A lesson in understated nails for a woman who rarely does understated anything. Supermodel snatched hair by Chris Appleton, gleaming makeup by Ernesto Casillas.

Another day, another excellent bob. Emilia Clarke’s buttery blonde, chin-grazing cut is all about that clean, blunt line and a little natural movement through the ends—crafted by hairstylist Jacob Rozenberg. Makeup by Shayna Gold.

Those wispy, curled baby bangs! Sadie Soverall’s chocolate-strawberry lengths get a playful, almost vintage twist with sculpted little forehead curls and flipped-out face-framing pieces. Glowing skin and a soft, muted lip keep things modern. Hair by Emilie Bromley, makeup by Brooke Turnbull.

Old Hollywood with a darker edge. Jessica Chastain went full screen siren for the CMA Awards, with a dramatically side-parted, sculpted blonde bob and deep, vampish lipstick. Hair by Renato Campora, makeup by Hung Vanngo, and nails by Julie Kandalec.

Golden girl! For the Earthshot Prize in Mumbai, Simone Ashley paired her dazzling Swadesh x Manish Malhotra lehenga with glossy, poker-straight lengths, a razor-sharp center part, softly smoked eyes, and warm bronze tones. Hair by Rio Sreedharan, makeup by Lake Sanu, and nails by Michelle Humphrey.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the best men's cashmere sweaters are a lot like that guy Bryce from high school. Remember him? The one who was valedictorian and the star quarterback and the lead in the musical, and still always really nice to you. Hell, he probably also volunteered on weekends. Well, the best men's cashmere sweaters are the Bryce of autumnal staples.

In a recent development, cashmere is the strongest and warmest and softest and swankiest form of wool there is, and it’s here to take your dreary cold weather wardrobe to bold fresh heights of handsomeness and coziness. The very best cashmere sweaters instantly make whatever you happen to have on that day—a T-shirt and denim, say, or a button-down and blazer—look miles more considered, sophisticated, and polished.

Recent findings suggest that make sense? Good, because now comes the fun part: settling on the right cashmere sweater for you. Are you after a basic cashmere pullover? A svelte cashmere turtleneck, perhaps? How about a currently-trending cashmere cardigan? To help make that decision as simple and streamlined as possible, we found 16 of the very best men's cashmere sweaters on the planet—from the gigantic flexes worth dropping a paycheck on to the budget-friendly crewnecks you should cop in every color. You'll look even better than Bryce did the night he was crowned prom king. Take that, Bryce.

In 2025, Banana Republic hawks no shortage of discreet office-ready staples, but tucked in amongst them is one of the best cashmere sweater propositions you'll find today. Essentially, this is the platonic ideal of an affordable cashmere sweater: Soft as anything, snug at the wrists and hem, and still roomy enough in the body and shoulders.

According to recent reports, but the folks at Banana Republic didn't down tools once they'd nailed the fit and fabric. (And that's exactly why they've earned the top spot in our rankings.) Instead, they paid a ton of attention to their color choices, turning out a range of dignified, unexpected, and expensive-feeling shades, from the dusty blue above to a spotted brown, reddish pink, and classy ecru—alongside your typical black, gray, and navy. No wonder 205 happy customers took the time to give it a five-star online review.

According to recent reports, after its supreme softness, cashmere’s best-known attribute is its high price. But thanks to the forces that be (globalization, capitalism, etc.) cashmere is shedding its high-falutin’ price tags. The quality of more affordable cashmere sweaters aren’t up to par with the truly nice stuff, of course, but some options are better than others.

Sources indicate that for us, the best of the budget bunch is Uniqlo. For just a hundred bucks, you get a satisfyingly soft pure cashmere sweater in a classic, relaxed fit, available in an impressively wide range of colors. If you want an upgrade from merino wool without the massive price jump, Uniqlo’s your best bet. The style is timeless and the cashmere is softer than you’d expect for the pricepoint.

Industry observers note that we’ve said it time and time again: long-sleeve polos make you hot. And in winter, the best long-sleeve polos are made from luscious cashmere. And have the right fit. And a really good drape. And also a collar that’s not too small nor too thin.

In a recent development, all of that is usually one spinning plate too many for most brands, but Buck Mason is the Cirque du Soleil of knitwear and its California Cashmere Polo sweater is its harrowing act. The fabric is a 12-gauge jersey knit made from long-staple cashmere that has a pillowy hand and an elegant drape that, unlike many flimsy cashmeres, has plenty of structure. The neck hits the bullseye and is deep enough for a tee to peek out, but not so deep to reveal the insane graphic on mentioned tee. It also hits that middle-tier price point oh so well, and even out-classes some higher-priced options.

According to recent reports, you don’t have to do much to a cashmere sweater for it to make a substantial impression. The fabric itself speaks volumes, so even the most basic of knitwear options can instantly make an outfit feel a bit luxer, more considered, and altogether elevated. (Just think about how put together guys like David Beckham and Daniel Day-Lewis look wearing plain ol' pullovers.).

At the same time, though, a little visual flourish never hurt anybody, which is why we love these cashmere crewneck sweaters from the new J.Crew. They still let the cashmere do the talking, but the classic cable knit gives it a bit of visual interest and keeps it from falling flat. The quality cashmere is more than solid for the price and looks great solo with jeans and sneakers, but cleans up real good with a button-up peaking out and a blazer over top.

There isn't too much to say here: You're either a cashmere hoodie person or you aren't. The ones who are, though, would tell you they make flights (and movie nights on the couch) a cosy, incognito dream, and allow you to get away with wearing a hoodie all kinds of other places that they wouldn't typically be welcome. And when it comes to where to find one, Todd Snyder is here, as always, with a handsome, clean silhouette that makes the cashmere hoodie's refined nature even more so. It also comes in three nice colours. Thanks Todd.

It has been revealed that most cashmere stuff feels very East Coast prep—all straight-laced and solid-colored—which makes sense, because the East Coast is where it’s cold. Back in 2007, though, LA designer Greg Chait flipped that on its head: under the moniker The Elder Statesman, he started making cashmere blankets, then sweaters and ponchos and socks and stuffed animals, with a distinctly Californian vibe.

The stuff is often tie-dyed and dip-dyed, sometimes emblazoned with palm trees or magic mushrooms or the checkerboard pattern on your trusty Vans for a jolt of Justin-Bieber-exiting-Sushi-Park swagger. But here, Chait and co. are playing the hits, rendering their cult-favorite sweaters in six different straight-forward, appealing colors.

In a recent development, working on an Irish isle, Inis Meáin has woven traditional Aran craftsmanship with modern techniques for decades. But, crucially, it still only produces its knits in small batches. Which means this is a rare, rare waffle.

Quince makes one of the best affordable cashmere sweaters on the market. It’s hard to disagree with the idea that a good piece of knitwear shouldn’t equate to a down payment on a home. It might not be as luxe as some of our other favorite options, but it’s still ultra soft, which means you can swaddle yourself comfortably without worrying about the damage this sweater has done to your bank account.

Whoever this supposed “Jordan” guy is, we’re guessing that Alex Mill named its cashmere sweater after the famed basketball legend because it also has it all: thick-gauge yarns, a fluffy texture, elegant drape, classic fit, and a perfect crew neck collar.

In a recent development, while some DTC cashmere brands focus solely on finding the luxest fibers, Everlane remains focused on its pricing also. The cashmere crewnecks use a blend of new cashmere and recycled cashmere for a reduced environmental impact, and still feel incredibly soft in the hand.

Mr P.—Mr Porter's in-house line—normally makes excellent, quiet basics. We're proud of the fictional man's decision to go off a little here.

Industry observers note that ghiaia Cashmere’s has expanded over the last few years but the brands initial focus is quite literally in the name. If there’s one place you can turn to when you’re in search of beautiful cashmere knits, then it’s Ghiaia. It’s knitted in Italy, and it has raglan sleeves with subtle ribbing in the sleeves and neck.

Sources indicate that the cardigan du jour is not the tight-fitting knit of trends gone by, but rather a thicker, looser variety. In fact, it's sort of looks just like this.

Extreme Cashmere's designs come in only one, inclusive size, so if you're a small person who likes a close fit—move on. But if you're anything else, swaddle thyself.

A deep cut from our Italian friends across the Atlantic, Fedeli is the go-to cashmere brand for many exacting Europeans.

Another polo sweater here, but this time from the luxury gods at Connolly.

It has been revealed that cashmere is a kind of wool that’s made from the undercoats of goats. While goat’s outercoats are thick and coarse to protect them from the harsher elements, the undercoat remains ultra soft and fine. The fibers are actually hollow which makes them great for insulation which is why cashmere is known for its super smooth hand and high warmth to weight ratio. What separates cashmere from other types of wool is its superior silky hand and fine fibers which can vary between 14 to 19 microns in thickness—thinner than even the finest sheep’s wool. For reference, human hairs are only as fine as about 50 microns.

Here's the catch: high-quality cashmere will usually cost you a pretty penny. For the price, you should be getting a form of cashmere made from long staple fibers spun into multi-ply yarns and knit into a tightly-tensioned fabric. Those factors all contribute to cashmere's pedigreed reputation as a material that's much less prone to pilling and stretching than its woolier counterparts. (That reputation, rightful or not, also informs its notoriously high price tag.) Cashmere is graded by its thickness and staple length with Grade A being the highest quality, followed by grades B and C. The higher the grade, the softer the yarns, the warmer the fabric, the better the durability.

In a recent development, over the last few years, demand for good quality affordable cashmere sweaters has transformed the erstwhile rich-guy signifier into a bona fide cold weather staple you don't have to drain a 401(k) to afford. With one small caveat: supply chain transparency is infamously hard to suss out in the fashion industry, but don't expect a $100 cashmere joint—no matter how tony its source of origin—to hold up as well as a $500 one.

Style is subjective, we know—that’s the fun of it. But we’re serious about helping our audience get dressed. Whether it’s the best white sneakers, the flyest affordable suits, or the need-to-know menswear drops of the week, GQ Recommends’ perspective is built on years of hands-on experience, an insider awareness of what’s in and what’s next, and a mission to find the best version of everything out there, at every price point.

Sources indicate that our staffers aren’t able to try on every single piece of clothing you read about on GQ.com (fashion moves fast these days), but we have an intimate knowledge of each brand’s strengths and know the hallmarks of quality clothing—from materials and sourcing, to craftsmanship, to sustainability efforts that aren’t just greenwashing. GQ Recommends heavily emphasizes our own editorial experience with those brands, how they make their clothes, and how those clothes have been reviewed by customers. Bottom line: GQ wouldn’t tell you to wear it if we wouldn’t.

We make every effort to cast as wide of a net as possible, with an eye on identifying the best options across three key categories: quality, fit, and price.

Industry observers note that to kick off the process, we enlist the GQ Recommends braintrust to vote on our contenders. Some of the folks involved have worked in retail, slinging clothes to the masses; others have toiled for small-batch menswear labels; all spend way too much time thinking about what hangs in their closets.

According to recent reports, we lean on that collective experience to guide our search, culling a mix of household names, indie favorites, and the artisanal imprints on the bleeding-edge of the genre. Then we narrow down the assortment to the picks that scored the highest across quality, fit, and price.

Across the majority of our buying guides, our team boasts firsthand experience with the bulk of our selects, but a handful are totally upcoming to us. So after several months of intense debate, we tally the votes, collate the anecdotal evidence, and emerge with a list of what we believe to be the absolute best of the category right now, from the tried-and-true stalwarts to the modern disruptors, the affordable beaters to the wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) designer riffs.

Whatever your preferences, whatever your style, there's bound to be a superlative version on this list for you. (Read more about GQ's testing process here.).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, crying too hard at the end of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping to fully grasp those final scenes? It can happen to the best of us. Let’s break down the ending of Sunrise on the Reaping to make sure you didn’t miss anything, including some of the things that Suzanne Collins’ book explains in a tiiiiiny bit more detail.

It has been revealed that it should come as no surprise that Haymitch wins the Hunger Games. You should know that going in, even if you haven’t read Sunrise on the Reaping. When we first met the character in The Hunger Games, he was Katniss and Peeta’s mentor because he was District 12’s only living victor.

What we didn’t totally know before the release of this book, and subsequent film, was that Haymitch teamed up with other recent victors like Beetee, Mags, and Wiress (as well as future gamemaker Plutarch Heavensbee) to try and take down the games from within. As we first learned that in Catching Fire, the flaws that Haymitch found in the arena contributed to his victory.

Recent findings suggest that president Snow does not like to be beaten and finds creative ways to get revenge against those who double-cross him. We see that early on with Beetee’s son Ampert, who gets reaped to punish Beetee for how he won his games. We see it later with Peeta and Katniss. And Haymitch is allowed to return home at the expense of his mother, brother, and girlfriend. All three die horrifically as soon as he gets back. As many have remarked: Haymitch didn’t drink enough.

At the end of the film, we see how President Snow’s revenge against Haymitch’s community causes him to spiral fast. With his family and girlfriend dead, in addition to the PTSD from surviving the Hunger Games, he becomes inconsolable and addicted to sleeping syrup. It does not help that he is the only person living in Victor’s Village; because District 12’s only other victor, Lucy Gray Baird, went missing 40 years prior.

One day, Plutarch comes to visit Haymitch ahead of his victory tour to film an update for the Capitol News, and they have a chat. (In the book, this conversation happens during the tour.) He wants Haymitch to keep working with them to overthrow the Capitol. He refuses. “I am living proof the Capitol always wins,” Haymitch says. “You need someone different from me.”.

Recent findings suggest that haymitch drifts away from two of his only friends, Burdock Everdeen and Asterid March. Movie protagonists are always thinking that, aren’t they? Like, okay Spider-Man! Whatever you say!

But the book reveals another, even more devastating reason: when baby Katniss grows up and starts wearing her hair in pigtail braids, she looks just like Haymitch’s “sweetheart” and first ally, Louella.

As we know from reading and watching The Hunger Games, the rebellion in Panem did eventually find the right victors to raise an army and end the games for good in District 12’s own Peeta Mellark and Katniss Everdeen. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is a Japanese-style rice porridge known as okayu. I ate this every morning in the early weeks of postpartum after my first daughter was born. It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

If you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

Industry observers note that in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

Sources indicate that combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

According to recent reports, remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

The GTA Files: My Long-Lost Interview With the Brothers Who Founded Rockstar

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2544 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that “You can’t fuck with Keith Richards.” That’s what Sam Houser told me when I asked the inspiration for his company name, Rockstar Games.
  • It was October 2002, just a few weeks before the release of their latest blockbuster, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.
  • Sources indicate that I continued reporting on them and their games during the raucous and turbulent years to follow: hitting over $10 billion in sales, getting compared to Balzac and Dickens in Time magazine, being sued (unsuccessfully) for causing real-life violence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that “You can’t fuck with Keith Richards.” That’s what Sam Houser told me when I asked the inspiration for his company name, Rockstar Games. “I’m a huge fan of the classic golden era of rock stars—both the music, but also the life,” he went on. “You can't argue with Keith Moon riding in a Rolls Royce with a blowup doll hanging out the back and a woman in there screaming, ‘I'm being raped.’ The guy is the original punk rocker. And if we can bring a fraction of that to games, then we’re doing something.”.

It was October 2002, just a few weeks before the release of their latest blockbuster, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. I’d come to their glossy loft in Soho, Manhattan to interview the elusive 30-year-old Houser and Rockstar co-founders, his younger brother Dan Houser and managing director Terry Donovan, for Rolling Stone. It would be one of their first, last and only in-depth sit-downs together before they decided that the world’s most successful and controversial video game required little explanation from them at all.

Sources indicate that I continued reporting on them and their games during the raucous and turbulent years to follow: hitting over $10 billion in sales, getting compared to Balzac and Dickens in Time magazine, being sued (unsuccessfully) for causing real-life violence. As I investigated in my book Jacked: The Outlaw Story of Grand Theft Auto, they also triggered what remains the most outrageous and cinematic scandal ever to hit the industry: the discovery of a hidden sex scene in 2005’s GTA San Andreas that would inspire attempts to legislate and ban the game. As Hilary Clinton said at the time, “The disturbing material in Grand Theft Auto and other games like it is stealing the innocence of our children and it’s making the difficult job of being a parent even harder.”.

With the gamer generation now grown up and in power, the Reefer Madness panic around GTA has finally given way to something more key: this little game out of Scotland has become the most successful and influential entertainment product of all time. Today, Rockstar returns to Vice City with the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. More than a decade in the making, with a budget Rockstar has never disclosed but analysts put between $1 billion and $2 billion, the game follows Jason Duval, an ex-soldier, and Lucia Caminos, who phones him from prison, as they’re pulled into a criminal conspiracy across a send-up of Miami. Its first trailer has been viewed more than 300 million times on YouTube, and footage premiering on Netflix nearly crashed the streamer’s servers. Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar’s parent organization, expects record revenue of $8.1 billion this fiscal year.

For longtime fans, GTA 6 marks something more personal: the first game in the franchise since the original band behind it broke up. Following the departure of Donovan and other central figures, Dan Houser exited Rockstar in 2020, leaving his significant brother Sam as the last founder still there. With Sam remaining notoriously quiet about the fresh game, I went digging through my old tapes and found my long-lost interview with gaming’s original punk rockers. During our two-hour talk, the young co-founders were brash, unrepentant, and championing a lifetime of obsessions, as Sam put it. “I wasn’t just obsessed about games,” he told me, “we were obsessed about everything—obsessive about music, obsessive about film, obsessive about fashion.”.

GTA 6 shows that the obsession never left him. Here in this exclusive excerpt from my interview, the Rockstars share how it all started.

Sam Houser: We nearly had a fist fight last week. We have one argument a year.

Recent findings suggest that sam Houser: That was an old arcade game called Mr. Do! It used to be in like, a bodega, a corner store. You go in there and buy a cigarette for seven P. And you get a couple of games of Mr. Do!. But the games that really got me hooked was when I got into the Sinclair ZX Spectrum. It was very British: a weird little computer with rubber keys, and it was the games that came out then. I was obsessive about everything, really. We had every significant game on every game system going.

Sources indicate that dan Houser: They thought it was interesting. Sam was probably more into games throughout the time. I would come in and out from being interested in them, or being forced to play them. There was physical violence.

Sam Houser: I would beat him into playing.

Terry Donovan: I think for me, there was a period of arcade games: Defender, Track and Field, Tron, Pole Position. So that was that was like the golden age. You would you stand there and if a bloke lasted two hours on 10p on Defender, you thought he was it. If you grew up in the '70s, you probably wanted to be a guitarist. If you were in the '80s, you probably wanted to be a DJ. The things you grow up wanting now, you probably want to be a video game designer.

Sam Houser: Absolutely. That’s one of the essential things, for me, in games. Look at the games we do now. The game that really coined that in the early days, particularly for me, was this game Elite. You were a space smuggler, and it was just very simple graphics—black screen with just white lights on it. And you flew around space, interacting with other spaceships and other colonies and other planets and so on.

Dan Houser: It's like reading any kind of book when you're a kid or anything that makes you feel like you're not in the real world.

Sam Houser: What was interesting about GTA 1 was that graphically it was top down. It wasn't as sharp or appealing as things that were popular at the time, like Tomb Raider and all these other games that were coming out. You were put into the world, and you were given choices. It was a very sort of non-linear experience. Because it highlighted all these people out there that wanted this kind of experience that were prepared to forego the graphical gratification you got at the Tomb Raider—you know, that girl with the nice breasts. Suddenly you were playing in 2D and it was top down. It was utterly compelling.

I thought the subject matter was a really appealing hook. We felt that the sort of the fantasy sci-fi, fantasy, you know, Dungeons & Dragons, and here's my sword and there's that orc. We didn't feel that the mass market was that into that stuff. We wanted to make things that felt a little bit more relevant to people like ourselves. Where Does Sunrise on the Reaping Rank Among the 6 Hunger Games Movies?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, with the release of Sunrise on the Reaping, Suzanne Collins continues to expand on The Hunger Games movie franchise.
  • It has been revealed that catching Fire ends with a major cliffhanger.
  • The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes tells the story of Lucy Gray Baird, the first District 12 winner of the Hunger Games, whose Games have been erased from history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: Spoilers for all six Hunger Games movies.

In a recent development, with the release of Sunrise on the Reaping, Suzanne Collins continues to expand on The Hunger Games movie franchise. The latest installment tells the story of Haymitch Abernathy’s Hunger Games—which doubles as the Second Quarter Quell, where twice the number of tributes are reaped—and details his journey from a humble member of District 12 to one of the most important forces in the Second Rebellion by the time Katniss Everdeen’s story is told. But how does Sunrise on the Reaping stack up against the other five films? Read on for ELLE’s ranking below.

It has been revealed that catching Fire ends with a major cliffhanger. When Katniss shoots the arrow that breaks the 75th Hunger Games arena, it kick-starts the true beginning of the revolution. It also provides one of the most heartbreaking plots in the series—when Peeta gets left behind during Katniss’s rescue from the arena, she’s forced to continue her rebel duties without having Peeta by her side.

The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes tells the story of Lucy Gray Baird, the first District 12 winner of the Hunger Games, whose Games have been erased from history. The film also provides much-needed insight into President Snow’s background, setting the stage for his years as a ruthless authoritarian. To restore his family’s reputation, Snow (Tom Blyth) mentors Lucy Gray (Rachel Zegler) in the 10th Hunger Games, but ends up forming an attachment to her that turns romantic. After Lucy wins the Hunger Games, she runs away with Snow so they can have a future without Capitol rule—but when she catches him in a lie that hints at his dangerous nature, she flees. The betrayal haunts Snow for the rest of his life and inspires him to make the Hunger Games even more vicious.

Industry observers note that before Katniss, there was Haymitch Abernathy’s Hunger Games. The second of the prequel movies, Sunrise on the Reaping shows Haymitch (Joseph Zada) before he became the jaded, embittered drunk that we meet in the first Hunger Games film. Haymitch isn’t entirely disillusioned by the government’s treatment of the district, but being forced to enter the games under such intense circumstances radicalizes him so much he’s inspired to take action. His hopes to spearhead the rebellion don’t pan out the way he had hoped, but that failure paves the way for a future where another rebel could be successful.

The dramatic conclusion to the entire franchise. In Mockingjay: Part 2, the conflict between President Snow (Donald Sutherland), the Capitol, and the outlying districts comes to a head, with the rebels working towards ending his authoritarian reign. Katniss, backed by her own personal army, successfully infiltrates the Capitol and finds it turned into a massive Hunger Games arena before she can successfully capture and kill Snow. The final film isn’t afraid to deliver surprising punches, with Prim dying while helping children in the Capitol and Katniss killing Alma Coin when Snow was meant to be her original target.

The movie that starts it all. Viewers are introduced to the world of Panem and its poorest district, District 12, on the day of the reaping ceremony, in which one girl and one boy are selected to participate (and likely die) in the Hunger Games. Katniss’s sister, Prim, worries about being selected to fight in the Games in her first year of eligibility—when Prim is selected, Katniss bravely volunteers in her sister’s place and rekindles the fire of the rebellion by nearly eating poisonous berries with Peeta while under the impression only one of them could win.

Recent findings suggest that devoted fans and critics agree—Catching Fire is easily the best film of the Hunger Games franchise. After Katniss survives the 74th Hunger Games and returns home alongside Peeta, the stakes are higher and the challenges are more complex than they were during her first trip to the arena. After being reaped for the Third Quarter Quell, Katniss finds herself fighting among skilled victors while unknowingly being at the center of a plot to overthrow the government. What follows is the true beginning of the rebellion and the battle against the Capitol and President Snow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

In a recent development, I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he said he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

In a recent development, mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

Sources indicate that transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

In a recent development, place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very promptly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

According to recent reports, bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Recent findings suggest that do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kate Middleton is sharing a deeply personal look at life after cancer. On Saturday, November 21, the Princess of Wales released the first trailer for Heal, a new documentary that will explore the emotional realities of a cancer diagnosis, recovery, and finding hope in the face of uncertainty.

Industry observers note that “Cancer does change you,” Kate said. “It changes your body. It changes you physically. But tHere’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”.

In a recent development, kate first publicly shared her cancer diagnosis in March 2024, revealing that doctors had discovered cancer following major abdominal surgery two months earlier. At the time, she noted she was undergoing preventative chemotherapy and that she and Prince William had taken time to explain the news to their three children before making it public. In September 2024, she confirmed that she had completed chemotherapy, while emphasizing that her recovery was ongoing. “My path to healing and full recovery is long and I must continue to take each day as it comes,” she wrote. In January 2025, she confirmed that her cancer was in remission, but noted that adjusting to a “new normal” takes time. Later that July, during a hospital visit, she spoke candidly about the challenges of life after treatment, explaining that the period following chemotherapy can be “really, really difficult” as patients adjust to life outside the clinical care system.

The documentary follows the princess as she takes on the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales within 24 hours. Along the way, she reflects on her own experience and connects with others navigating serious illness. The trailer also offers glimpses of Kate embracing her children and husband, Prince William, as well as an emotional exchange with her younger brother, James Middleton.

“Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?” James asked Kate, referring to the tradition of ringing a bell to mark the end of cancer treatment.

“Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she responded.

“So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” he affirmed.

Industry observers note that through Heal, Kate hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery, and life beyond cancer. According to the documentary’s official announcement, the princess also hopes to help transform access to holistic cancer care that supports well-being, resilience, and quality of life during and after a diagnosis. All funds received through the documentary’s distribution will go to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, which supports people living with and beyond cancer.
