📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Surveying the best zip-up hoodies for men takes me back to my younger days as a hopelessly romantic high school kid. My formative years were marred by angst, soundtracked by pop punk, emo, and indie rock. The piece of clothing that got me through it all? A zip-up hoodie. It was core to the indie aesthetic, with every forlorn frontman sporting one over a thrashed band tee, skinny jeans, and shredded Chucks. But nostalgia never seems to stay in the past, especially when fashion is involved.

Gen-Z has revived every minute piece of 2000s pop culture, which means zip-up hoodies are back and have all but usurped the pullover hoodie as the sweat du jour. The zip-up is inherently versatile in both practical wear and sheer styling dexterity. With the flick of the zip, you can put your beloved Death Cab for Cutie tee on full display while letting your pits breathe, or keep it zipped up when it's just a bit too nippy out. To find the best zip-up hoodies on the market, I dusted off Transatlanticism and went on a deep dive. The good news is that the old classics are still good. The better news is that there's a lot of great competition to choose from.

Uniqlo’s no-nonsense clean aesthetic and low price point has made it a go-to for any menswear enjoyer looking for good style on a budget. While the brand excels at cashmere sweaters, T-shirts, and a slew of homerun collabs, the Japanese label’s sweats are criminally underrated. We’d go so far as to say that they should be talked in the same breath as brands like Champion and Sunspel. This zip up hoodie took us by surprise thanks to its comfy midweight, all-cotton fabric and solid construction. But the main selling point is the impeccable fit.

So many other brands cut their hoodies too long in the body and leave you looking like Jack Skellington’s pubescent brother. Uniqlo managed to cut its French terry hoodie to sit right at the hips which makes for a more classic and natural silhouette that’s neither lanky nor sloppy. Because of the fabric, the feel, and the overall fit, this is my favorite zip-up hoodie by a sizable margin. It’s my most-worn hoodie and has yet to show signs of any fraying.

In a recent development, hoodies were originally meant for sportswear, as warm up gear before a grueling game of football. These days, they’re more often worn for lounging on the couch to watch the kickoff. And if you want to kick it in comfort while saving your pennies for booze and amuse bouche for the major game with the boys, the best budget zip up hoodie to buy is Hanes’ EcoSmart zip hoodie. The fit is spot on—relaxed, but not sloppy, comfy in the body and the sleeves without swallowing you like a sand pit.

It has been revealed that the fit is impressive for the price, and the overall quality means you’re getting a little more than what you pay for. It’s not a hoodie that’ll last you for too long, but it is a good quality piece for just 15 bucks. And when other hoodies offer lesser quality and worse-fitting options for about the same price? The answer is clear.

It’s hard not to sing the praises of Reigning Champ, a brand that built its fleece empire on sweatpants and hoodies. The Canadian label’s flagship midweight terry fabric has drawn the attention of streetwear royalty and menswear buffs alike and its dedication to quality has elevated the humble hoodie to oxygen-deprived heights. We named Reigning Champ’s crewneck sweatshirt and pullover hoodie as among our favorites in their respective categories, and the same goes for its zip-up hooded sweatshirt. It’s made of the same 100% cotton French terry fabric as its superlative-earning brethren and is cut with high-quality flatlock stitching for a smooth, un-bulky feel.

I had high expectations for Reigning Champ, given my previous experience, and I’m not surprised at all with how nice this zip-up is. And while I'm partial to the standard fit, it’s also available in a slim fit version, too.

Hoodies live in a universe well beyond the sportswear world from which they originated. And while we still enjoy the OGs and the classics that made the hoodie a bona fide menswear must-have, we also love seeing all the ways the style has been pushed, tweaked, and freaked. Our Legacy's Level Hood has been a successful avenue for the Stockholm-based brand to explore the limits of the hoodie and this particular version strikes a delicate balance between the freaky and the fashion-curious. It's made of an English wool knit into an all-over ribbed texture for a throwback '90s feel. The cropped, boxy silhouette and elongated sleeves harken back to the grunge-y era, while the sultry dual-tone nightshade colorway throws you off in the best way possible.

Sources indicate that menswear influencers will be happy to regale you with their TedTalk on the golden ratio of clothing proportions. Essentially, that means your outfit should be divided into three equal sections where the top takes up one third of the outfit. Basically, your tops should be cropped and sit closer to your natural waist. Follow it up with some high-waisted pants with a wide silhouette and you’ve instantly garnered 300K views on TikTok (RIP). With so many indie brands and influencers scrambling to make their own versions of “the perfect cropped hoodie” you’re probably tired of wading through all the choices. Do yourself a favor and go to Abercrombie.

The Moose’s version is backed by actual trend forecasters, actual designers, and actual fit models. What does that mean, exactly? It means that its cropped zip hoodie fits really well and uses surprisingly beefy fabric. It was a revelation for me, too—Abercrombie wasn’t a name I associated with hoodies, but after I saw this in person, I had to readjust my menswear word cloud.

Some of the best zip-up hoodies for men are made by a brand you never see in brick and mortar stores. Camber has been crafting the most durable sweats for decades, right here in America and have been the shining example of the difference between good quality and great quality. Sure, you have to order through an old-school web 1.0 website and wait for several weeks to actually get your hoodie. But trust us when we say that the relatively minor inconvenience is completely worth it.

The heavyweight fleece is almost as thick as a leather jacket and can stand in as outerwear if you wanted it to. While other hoodies are washed to hell in giant industrial washing machines to reach a super soft texture by the time it gets to you, Camber’s actually require you to do the work yourself. It sort of feels like you’re being swaddled by an anaconda, which means if you’re a proponent of hard clothes like raw denim, you’ll like Camber’s hoodie a lot.

Cashmere zip hoodies, once the exclusive province of Silicon Valley unicorn founders and PJ-flying nepo babies, have been democratized, none better than Naadam's take. You know the brand for bringing thoughtful, sustainable cashmere pieces at “really, only that much?” prices. Its zip hoodie is as soft as it gets, with extra credit points awarded for coming in a classic fit (too many cashmere hoodies err on the side of slim) and six colors, including this decidedly handsome olive. Wear it on weekends, work-from-home Fridays, and long flights—even if it's just Economy+.

In a recent development, shoutout to brother in arms Louis Cheslaw, GQ Recs contributor, whose writing for the newsletter Magasin put us on to young brand Cease. From seed to sewing, it's beefy 20-ounce cotton is fully American-made. Assembling the fabric vertically means the hoodie will shorten up to a slightly cropped, oversized fit. Act fast if you want some of the less-boring colors—they move fast.

We can’t deny Russell Athletic’s contributions to the hoodie space. And while its formula has changed over the years, the new hoodies are still pretty good for the price. The fabric is soft and lightweight, and it’s available in a rainbow of colorways. Plus, if you’re looking for a hoodie with a little more length, this is a great option.

It has been revealed that bold graphics aren’t usually deemed classics, but Gap’s retro-leaning collegiate-style block logo has staying power almost as much as the Levi’s red tab. Add to that a wonderfully fluffy midweight fleece material and a tailored straight fit and you’ve got something you’ll see on moodboards for generations to come.

Recent findings suggest that champion’s Reverse Weave fabric is iconic for its nearly shrink-proof quality and almost unsettlingly rough exterior. Flip it to the inside and you’ve got a luxuriously brushed interior that’ll have you feeling like you’re melting into a cloud. Heads-up that pricing varies kinda wildly by size on Amazon.

The secondhand market is chock full of navy-blue hoodies that have been sun-faded and beaten down with time. They'll cost you just as much as this Mfpen version, but will also fall apart faster than you can zip 'em up.

Les Tien's dedication to all things sweats results in a catalog of luxurious fleece and terry cloth with a modern approach. Featuring high-end Cobrax hardware, RiRi zippers, raw-edge hems and sleeves, and a heavyweight brushed fleece, no detail is phoned in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pavlova is essentially a massive meringue that melts in your mouth. We top our version with whipped cream and fresh berries for an airy and fruity bite that will keep you coming back bite after bite. It may look like a complicated dessert made by only the best chefs, but it's surprisingly easy to make! You just need some patience. The key to perfection is drying it out, which requires you to leave it in a (turned-off) oven overnight after it bakes.

If you’re looking for something a bit more festive, check out our Christmas wreath pavlova for a holiday spin on the classic.

Arrange a rack in the center of the oven; preheat to 300°. In a large bowl, beat egg whites with a large pinch of salt on medium-high speed with a handheld mixer (or in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment) until foamy, which should take about one minute.

While beating, slowly add sugar and beat until meringue is thick and glossy, which should take about 7 minutes. Beat in vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla until well combined.

It has been revealed that pile the meringue in the center of a parchment-lined baking sheet. Using a spatula or spoon, spread the mixture into an 8" circle. Make a small well in the center.

Transfer to the oven, and immediately reduce the oven temperature to 250°. Bake the meringue until set but still white, which should take about an hour. Turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely in the oven for at least 2 hours and up to overnight. Transfer cooled pavlova to a platter.

Top with whipped cream and berries.

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

Sources indicate that store the unassembled pavlova in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, keeping it away from humidity. Once topped with whipped cream and fresh fruit, refrigerate and enjoy within a day, as the meringue will soften over time.

How to Survive Politics Talk at Thanksgiving (Without Losing Your Mind)

💡 Key Takeaways

  • While tapping out of politics talk entirely doesn’t feel like an option in 2026, it feels equally dismal to simply accept a tense or outright hostile environment during what should be a joyful and grateful time of year.
  • For some expert guidance on this matter, Vogue spoke to Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, thanksgiving is almost upon us, and given that we’re fresh off a midterms blue wave in the US, it’s probably not realistic to expect the holiday to be totally free of political drama. (Unless every member of your family is magically politically aligned on every matter, but when has that ever happened?).

While tapping out of politics talk entirely doesn’t feel like an option in 2026, it feels equally dismal to simply accept a tense or outright hostile environment during what should be a joyful and grateful time of year. Personally, I can vouch for the strategy of finding small political-adjacent moments to unite over, even if they feel frivolous—for example, your DSA-member sister and your establishment-Democrat mom may not align on all of Latest York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s policies, but you can probably get them both to agree that watching him personally shovel New Yorkers’ snow last winter was adorable.

For some expert guidance on this matter, Vogue spoke to Dr. Audra Nuru, a professor of communication and family studies at the University of St. Thomas in St. Paul, Minnesota, about how to engage loved ones with differing views in a productive way (and, just as importantly, how to set boundaries when it feels like engagement is no longer good for you and your mental health). Find her thoughts—and some sample scripts she's provided for different conversations—below.

Vogue: How do you recommend preparing for an event or gathering that might include viewpoints you disagree with or find harmful?

It has been revealed that dr. Audra Nuru: It’s true that those kinds of encounters can benefit from a bit of preparation. I like to think of it like packing for a trip to a new and unfamiliar place—you want to be prepared for the expected, but also pack with an open mind for the unexpected. So, before heading into that event, take some time to reflect on what topics might feel a bit sensitive for you, almost like checking the weather forecast, so you can pack accordingly. Remember, everyone is coming to the table with their own unique experiences and perspectives. Embrace those differences with curiosity and kindness. And of course, it’s always wise to set healthy boundaries—that’s like having a good map and a reliable guide to help you navigate any unfamiliar territory.

Is there a subtle, useful way to redirect a political conversation that's starting to feel upsetting?

According to recent reports, first and foremost, prioritize the relationship. Remember that the person you’re talking to matters more than proving a point. Ask yourself, “How can I express my views while still showing respect and valuing this person?” Part of showing respect is acknowledging that you may have different perspectives. If a conversation starts to feel a little uncomfortable, try gently saying something like, “I hear you, and I hold a different perspective.” This lets the other person know you’re listening and that their views matter, even if you don’t agree.

Recent findings suggest that secondly, listen with your heart, not just your head. Truly try to understand where they’re coming from, even if you disagree. What experiences have shaped their beliefs? What emotions are they expressing? And remember, even when it’s tough, try to see things from their perspective. Stepping into another’s shoes, even for a moment, can foster understanding and empathy.

Third, look for points of connection. Even in the midst of disagreement, there’s often some shared experiences or common ground to connect on. It can also be valuable to sense when a conversation needs a pause. If things are starting to feel tense, it’s completely fine to suggest taking a break or shifting to a different topic. Ultimately, navigating difficult conversations with respect is about how we connect, even when we disagree. It’s about building bridges of understanding by making space for different perspectives.

What’s a respectful yet firm way to let someone know their comments have crossed a line?

It has been revealed that using “I” language is such a powerful tool for navigating difficult conversations. Instead of pointing fingers, “I” language lets us shift the focus to our own experience. Imagine saying something like, “I felt uncomfortable when I heard that comment.” It’s honest, it’s respectful, and it avoids making the other person feel attacked. When we own our feelings, it invites the other person to do the same. It creates this space for empathy and understanding, even when we might disagree.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A big, billowing cloud of meringue tops this crimson beauty and acts as a sweet reprieve from the tart cranberry curd. The vibrant filling is made even more sour with a generous amount of lime juice. Think lemon meringue pie but holiday-ified. Use our Perfect Pie Crust as the base to create a sturdy-flaky foundation, and be sure to start the pie the day before you strategy to serve it, as the curd requires several hours of chilling to set into a sliceable texture. Cut into it too soon and it will run onto your plate, creating a messy—albeit delicious—slice.

We never make pie dough without a metal bench scraper. Our favorite is from Gestura. Use the scraper to cut butter, fold dough and nudge it into shape, transfer it from counter to plastic wrap, trim edges, cut strips, and, sure, scrape flour off your counter.

In a recent development, welcome to Bon Appétit Bake Club, a community of curious bakers. Each month senior Test Kitchen editors Jesse Szewczyk and Shilpa Uskokovic share a must-make recipe and dive deep on why it works. Come bake and learn with us—ask questions, share pics, listen to our podcast, and lots more here. And don't forget to join the Bake Club Group chat over on Substack.

3 hours (plus 30 minutes for freezing and 5 hours for chilling).

Sources indicate that whisk 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour, 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ¼ tsp. baking powder in a large bowl to combine. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces, and rub into dry ingredients with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy). Add 10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash with your fingers into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea-size).

Make a well in the center of mixture and pour in ¼ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute, then knead in bowl a couple of times to bring dough together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn out dough onto a surface lightly dusted with rice flour or all-purpose flour and dust top of dough with flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold dough in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting with more rice flour as needed to prevent sticking. Pat into a ½"-thick disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

Let dough disk sit at room temperature 5 minutes. Roll out dough on a lightly floured surface to a 12" round, about ¼" thick. Brush excess flour from dough and wrap around rolling pin. Transfer to a 9"-diameter pie pan (such as East Fork Spun Iron Pie Dish). Unfurl into pan, then lift edges and allow dough to slump down into pan. Trim, leaving about a 1½" overhang. Fold overhang under so crust is flush with edges of pan and crimp as desired with lightly floured fingers. Set pan on a rimmed baking sheet and prick bottom and sides of crust with a fork in several places. Freeze, uncovered, at least 30 minutes and up to 2 hours.

It has been revealed that place a rack in lower third of oven; preheat to 400°. Line crust with a sheet of parchment paper and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake crust, tenting edges with foil if browning too promptly, until edges are set and look dry, 20–25 minutes. Carefully lift out parchment paper and weights and continue baking crust, gently pressing bottom and sides occasionally with a flat-bottomed measuring cup if puffing up, until bottom looks dry and is golden, 20–25 minutes more. Transfer pan to a wire rack and let crust cool.

Industry observers note that do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

Bring 1 lb. fresh or frozen cranberries, 1½ cups (300 g) granulated sugar, and ¼ cup water to a boil in a large saucepan, then reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring often, until cranberries soften and burst and most of the liquid has evaporated, 10–15 minutes. Let cranberry mixture cool.

It has been revealed that transfer cranberry mixture to a blender; reserve pan. Add ⅔ cup fresh lime juice and ¼ cup (32 g) cornstarch and blend on high speed until smooth. Scrape purée back into pan (not over heat) and add 3 large eggs, 2 large egg yolks, 1 Tbsp. vanilla extract, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt. Place over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until mixture bubbles and thickens to a pudding-like consistency, about 4 minutes. Remove pan from heat. Add ¾ cup (1½ sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces, and whisk until melted and combined. Strain curd through a fine-mesh sieve, pushing with a rubber spatula, directly into crust. Smooth into an even layer and cover with plastic wrap, pressing directly onto surface. Chill pie at least 4 hours and up to 1 day.

Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment on medium speed until foamy and sugar is dissolved, about 5 minutes. Listen, we all know that stuffing is the best part of Thanksgiving dinner, but because of the butter, eggs, and chicken broth that usually go into classic stuffing, it's a dish that vegans can't always enjoy—until now! We created a stuffing that's so delicious, you might even be convinced to make a few of your other holiday classics into vegan Thanksgiving versions.

According to recent reports, start your stuffing off by preheating the oven to 200° and slicing the bread into roughly 1” cubes. Spread the cubes in a single layer on a large baking sheet and bake for about 20 minutes, until the bread is nice and crisp.

It has been revealed that remove the bread from the oven and turn the temperature up to 350°. Grease a 13” x 9” baking dish with cooking spray and heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion to the skillet and cook for about 5 minutes until lightly charred in some spots, then add the celery and garlic and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the celery starts to turn translucent. Pour in the vegetable stock and scrape up any browned bits—this is where all the flavor is. Season with salt and pepper.

Mix the bread cubes and chopped herbs in the vegetable stock mixture until well combined, then transfer to the prepared baking dish.

Recent findings suggest that cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil and place it in the oven to bake for 40 minutes. Carefully remove the foil and continue baking for another 35 minutes, until the stuffing is golden brown and crisp on top.

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

It has been revealed that looking for more vegan holiday inspo? Whip up our cauliflower stuffing for a low-carb option, or try out our vegetarian mushroom gravy or vegan mashed potatoes to truly complete your spread!

Recent findings suggest that any leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. You can also prepare this dish ahead of time, as it’s the kind of dish that we think tastes even better after sitting for a day.

Whisk 3⅓ cups (417 g) all-purpose flour, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ½ tsp. baking powder in a large bowl to combine. Add 4 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces; rub into dry ingredients with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy). Add 1¼ cups (2½ sticks) chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash with your fingers into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea-size).

Sources indicate that make a well in the center of mixture and pour in ½ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute, then knead in bowl a couple of times to bring dough together (some dry bits may remain).

Industry observers note that turn out dough onto a surface lightly dusted with rice flour or all-purpose flour; dust top of dough with flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold dough in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting with more flour as needed to prevent sticking. Divide dough in half and pat each piece into a ½"-thick disk. Wrap each disk tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

According to recent reports, do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap each disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

Place 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar and ½ cup water in a medium Dutch oven or other heavy pot and cover. Bring to a boil over medium heat (no need to stir); cook until sugar is dissolved, 4–7 minutes total. Uncover and continue to cook, stirring or swirling pot occasionally, until caramel turns a deep golden brown, 10–12 minutes.

In a recent development, add zest of 1 lemon, 3 lb. Honeycrisp apples (about 6 large), peeled, cored, quartered, thinly sliced crosswise, ½ cup bourbon, 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. ground cinnamon to caramel (it may become stiff). Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until caramel dissolves and apples have released a generous amount of liquid and are tender but still retain their shape (they should look mostly translucent), 15–18 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that stir ⅓ cup heavy cream, 3 Tbsp. cornstarch, and 2 Tbsp. cool water in a small bowl until cornstarch is dissolved. Pour into apple mixture and cook (it should be bubbling), stirring often, until mixture is thick, about 5 minutes. Transfer filling to a large bowl; let cool. Cover and chill until cold, at least 45 minutes.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, let dough sit at room temperature 5 minutes. Unwrap 1 disk and roll out on a surface lightly dusted with rice flour or all-purpose flour to a 12" round, about ¼" thick. Brush excess flour from dough and wrap around rolling pin. Transfer to a 9"-diameter pie pan (such as East Fork Spun Iron Pie Dish). Unfurl into pan, then lift edges and allow dough to slump down into pan. Trim, leaving about a 1" overhang. Chill 15 minutes.

It has been revealed that unwrap remaining disk; roll out on surface lightly dusted with more rice flour to a 18x12" rectangle, about ⅛" thick. Brush excess flour from dough and transfer to a large parchment-lined baking sheet. Brush dough with a thin film of cold water; sprinkle remaining ¼ cup (50 g) granulated sugar over and press gently with your hands to cover dough completely in an even layer (coating dough before cutting into strips will give you the most even coverage). Chill 15 minutes.

Industry observers note that place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 375°. Spoon chilled filling into pie pan and smooth surface to level. Using a ruler, cut dough rectangle into 1"-wide strips. Lay 5–8 strips over filling, spacing evenly across surface to cover. Weave another 5–8 strips over, then under, alternating to create a lattice crust (you may not use all of the strips). Trim overhang to match bottom crust. Press edges of top and bottom crusts firmly together to seal, then trim again, leaving about ¼" overhang. Fold overhang up and over lattice so crust is flush with edges of pan and crimp as desired with lightly floured fingers.

Place pan on a rimmed baking sheet (to catch drips) and bake pie until crust is set and golden, 45–50 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 350°; continue to bake until crust is deep golden brown and filling is bubbling up through lattice, 40–50 minutes more. Transfer pan to a wire rack and let pie cool in pan at least 4 hours before serving.

According to recent reports, do Ahead: Filling can be made 2 days ahead; keep chilled. Pie can be baked 1 day ahead; store, loosely covered, at room temperature.

Chicken Francese is a staple at your favorite Italian restaurants. But sometimes, you don't want to empty your wallet for this classic dinner favorite. That's where I come in! Francese is a preparation (much like Milanese) that can be used with all types of meat and seafood, from shrimp to veal. For chicken, it involves dredging cutlets in flour and beaten egg, creating a pseudo-batter. The cutlets are then pan-fried and made crispy, albeit temporarily. See, chicken Francese is one of those dishes that epitomizes "crispy gone soggy"—a texture sensation that is one of my absolute favorites. In this case, the chicken becomes "soggy" because you finish them by simmering it in a rich, lemony sauce that will knock your socks off.

Industry observers note that it might seem strange, but it’s such an iconic flavor/texture combination. Also, it is very easy to make and comes together in under an hour. What could be better?!

Industry observers note that place 1 chicken breast on a cutting board. Using a sharp chef’s knife held parallel to the cutting board, slice into the thickest side of the breast, cutting three-quarters of the way through. Fold the top piece back (as if you were opening a book) and continue to cut until the breast is divided into 2 thinner cutlets. Repeat with the remaining chicken breast for a total of 4 cutlets. Working one piece at a time, place each cutlet between 2 sheets of plastic wrap. Using a meat mallet or the bottom of a small heavy skillet, pound the chicken to about 1/4" thick. Season all over with salt and pepper.

Recent findings suggest that in a shallow dish, beat eggs, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt. Pour 1/2 cup flour into another shallow dish.

In a large, heavy skillet over medium heat, heat oil. Working in batches, coat cutlets in flour, shaking off excess, then dip into the egg mixture, turning to coat.

Place cutlets in the oil, being careful not to overcrowd the skillet, and cook, turning halfway through, until golden brown, 5 to 7 minutes.

Transfer cutlets to a paper towel-lined plate to drain and season with salt and pepper.

Wipe out the skillet, then heat over medium heat. Add five Tbsp. butter and the remaining one Tbsp. flour, stirring until just beginning to foam and the butter is melted, 3 to 5 minutes. Whisk in wine. Increase heat to medium-high and bring to a boil. Cook, stirring, until slightly reduced, 1 to 2 minutes. Add stock, lemon zest, and lemon juice and return to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and cook, whisking constantly, until the sauce is reduced by about one-third, 3 to 5 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add lemon slices and remaining 1 Tbsp. butter and cook, stirring, until the sauce is glossy, 2 to 3 minutes more.

Return chicken to the sauce and cook, turning halfway through, until heated through, 2 to 3 minutes.

Transfer chicken to a platter and pour the sauce over. Top with lemon slices and parsley.

It has been revealed that if you have any leftovers, store them in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Luckily, this dish is used to being a tad soggy and lends itself well to being reheated in the microwave.

Sources indicate that costume designer Mirren Gordon-Crozier, who counts the mid-century Lessons in Chemistry and the hyper-contemporary Margo’s Got Money Troubles among her credits, has no trouble flitting between eras. But Netflix’s latest hit, The Body, a coming-of-age psychological drama set at a Catholic high school in 2004, posed a latest challenge. “I hadn’t done that period before, even though I lived in it,” Gordon-Crozier tells Vogue. “I was about these girls’s age during that time. I sort of know all these girls, in a way. I think we all do, maybe.”.

Recent findings suggest that gordon-Crozier grew up in London and moved to Upcoming York to attend Parsons School of Design, where she adapted to American culture by discerning what signaled status to her classmates. “Having a Balenciaga bag was really key, and that was my main takeaway from college,” she jokes. The City bag does indeed make an appearance, as do a host of other It bags—the Dior Saddle and Louis Vuitton x Takashi Murakami Pochette among them.

“Everything about that era was very important to me because it was also when I was 18 and understanding how you could bond with someone over fashion,” Gordon-Crozier says. Indeed, on-screen interloper Lisbeth (Geena Meszaros) uses fashion to mark her shift from Pentecostal outsider to dance team member. But Gordon-Crozier notes that, although Lisbeth’s sartorial transformation follows her character arc, she ends the season still an outcast. “I think she doesn’t really know about pop culture or any sort of contemporary references at all. I think she was just emulating whatever Anya (Kristina Bogic) was doing,” she says.

Industry observers note that A stint at Catholic school also informed Gordon-Crozier’s approach to the costumes. “The way to show your personal style is very minute, since everyone’s skirt has to be the same,” she says. Both on The Body and at her school, girls would roll or alter their skirts to raise the hemline and accessorize their uniforms with designer bags and jewelry. But Gordon-Crozier and creator Quinn Shephard gave themselves an extra challenge. “We set constraints for ourselves: no makeup, no jewelry. Only religious jewelry,” she explains.

Industry observers note that one area where there was no room for even subtle individuality? The cutout leotards festooned with teal sequins that the Lions wear as their dance competition costumes. “The girls were not happy about those costumes, let’s just say that,” Gordon-Crozier laughs. “I’m like, You’re not supposed to be happy with them, okay?”.

Sources indicate that the inspiration came from a surprisingly fashionable source. “I saw this image of Chloë Sevigny in a cutout black bodysuit, probably around the same year,” she says. “It was just with a low-waisted strappy thing—very early 2000s.” Et voilà: with matching dance shoes, thick nude tights in just the wrong shade (Gordon-Crozier notes they are the same brand that Hooters uses for its uniforms), and hair rhinestones, they had the perfect ugly dance costume. “We wanted it to be as tacky as possible, like dance competitions are,” she says.

Offstage, though, Gordon-Crozier assigned each of the girls on the dance team a specific celebrity or pop star to emulate. “Anya always felt like Misha Barton and Sienna Miller, Elise (Sara Boustany) had a lot of Devon Aoki, and then Maddie (Shirley Chen) is Hillary Duff,” she indicates. “We tried to define every one of them. It just makes it easier when you’re shopping and putting looks together. Everyone has their own color palette, so they’re not really clashing.”.

Recent findings suggest that gordon-Crozier had a particular fondness for Elise’s edgier wardrobe. “Sara personally also has very similar tastes in a way: She likes dark and edgy designers like Comme des Garçons and Plein Sud and Diesel,” she claims. It was Boustany’s personal tastes that helped bolster the character of Elise to feel less like a Y2K totem and more like a real person. “I had references for her, but I feel like what we made was more unique. It came alive in the fittings rather than completely copying references.”.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Bonappetit ↗ Open Full Page

How to Blind-Bake Pie Crust—and When You Need To

📅 16 May 2016 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1460 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bonappetit

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the road to pie perfection is paved in pitfalls.
  • Recent findings suggest that but getting the crust to the right color depends on what you’re planning to fill it with.
  • Recent findings suggest that blind baking is especially useful when the filling needs less time in the oven than the crust does.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the road to pie perfection is paved in pitfalls. I’ve fallen into plenty of them throughout my baking career. The infamous “soggy bottom” is among the most common, but it’s easy to avoid. Blind baking—baking the crust before adding the filling—helps prevent an underbaked crust by giving the pastry a head start in the oven or cooking it completely before the filling goes in.

Recent findings suggest that but getting the crust to the right color depends on what you’re planning to fill it with. A pale, partially baked shell might be perfect for one pie, while another needs a deep golden brown crust before you add even a spoonful of filling. Here’s how to know when enough color is enough.

Recent findings suggest that blind baking is especially useful when the filling needs less time in the oven than the crust does. For custard pies, like pumpkin pie, partially baking the shell gives the pastry a head start so it doesn’t end up uncooked beneath a set filling. For pies with no-bake fillings, such as chocolate pudding pie or cranberry curd pie, the crust needs to be fully baked before it’s filled.

It has been revealed that most traditional fruit pies don’t need blind baking. Their fillings and crusts spend enough time in the oven together for the pastry to cook through. There are exceptions, particularly single-crust fruit pies topped with a crumble. Our Peach-Blueberry Pie, for example, starts with a thoroughly blind-baked shell before the filling goes in. Follow your recipe’s instructions rather than assuming every fruit pie needs the same treatment.

Start with a good pie dough. Roll it out, fit it into the pie plate, and crimp the edge. Chill the shaped shell for at least 15 minutes before baking; cold dough holds its shape better in the oven, reducing the risk of shrinking or slumping.

According to recent reports, next, line the shell with parchment paper and fill it with pie weights. Crumpling the parchment first, then unfolding it, helps it conform to the shell. The weights hold the dough against the pan while it bakes, preventing the bottom from puffing up and the sides from collapsing.

It has been revealed that you can buy ceramic pie weights or use dried beans, rice, or stainless-steel ball bearings. I’m partial to the ball bearings: They’re small enough to settle into the corners of the pie plate and heavy enough to hold the dough firmly in place.

Industry observers note that not everyone in the Bon Appétit Test Kitchen agrees. Editors Jesse Szewczyk and Rebecca Firkser prefer lighter alternatives. In their experience, heavy metal weights can compress the dough, limiting the expansion of the buttery layers that make pie crust flaky. Jesse uses dried beans or rice; Rebecca prefers dried chickpeas or even granulated sugar, a technique popularized by baking expert Stella Parks.

All of these options can work. Whichever you choose, fill the parchment-lined shell generously, supporting the sides all the way to the rim. Leave the weights in place until the crust looks dry and set and the parchment releases easily; removing them too soon can cause the sides to slump.

Our Cranberry Meringue Pie has a fully blind-baked pie crust.

It has been revealed that this method uses our Perfect Pie Crust dough and makes one 9"-diameter pie shell. It produces an evenly golden crust; if your pie calls for a paler or more deeply browned shell, follow its specific baking instructions and use the visual guide below.

According to recent reports, some pie recipes call for docking (pricking the bottom and sides of the dough with a fork) before baking. This allows steam to escape and helps prevent uneven puffing, but doesn’t replace the support of pie weights. Follow your recipe’s instructions; docking isn’t necessary for every blind-baked crust.

Sources indicate that do Ahead: A fully blind-baked crust can be made up to 2 days ahead. Let cool completely, wrap well, and store at room temperature until ready to fill.

Sources indicate that the short answer: It depends on what you’re putting inside. Some pies need only a partially baked crust, while others call for a shell that’s deeply golden brown.

Oven temperatures vary, different pie plates conduct heat differently, and the filling determines how much additional baking the crust will get. Use the recipe’s timing as a guide, but watch the color and texture of the pastry. Here’s what to look for.

Recent findings suggest that fruit pies need a pale base because they bake a looong time. Or at least, that’s often the thinking. If you’re making a single-crust variety topped with a crumble, such as our Blueberry Crumble Pie, and the recipe calls for blind-baking, you might want to start with an anemic crust. It’ll have plenty of time to brown as the juices thicken.

A pale, partially baked crust should look set rather than raw. The bottom should look set and opaque with some light golden patches, while the crimped edge may already be noticeably browned. The crust will continue to develop color once the filling goes in.

According to recent reports, don’t assume fruit pies always need a pale shell. Our Peach-Blueberry Pie, for example, calls for a well-browned crust before the fruit and crumble go in. And many double-crust fruit pies don’t need blind baking at all.

Industry observers note that A lightly baked shell can also be appropriate for custards that have a substantial bake ahead. BA’s Best Pumpkin Pie starts with a partially baked crust before the custard goes in for at least another hour.

The goal is to give the crust enough of a head start without taking it so far that the edges burn before the filling finishes cooking.

Custard pies, such as chess and our Lemon Buttermilk Pie, often have shorter bake times than fruit pies, so the crust needs a solid golden base layer to develop enough color by the time the filling sets.

Here, you’re looking for more than a crust that’s simply dry and set. The bottom should be evenly golden with no pale, translucent patches, and the sides should have taken on some color too. The rim will generally be a little darker than the bottom, but the whole shell should look well on its way to being fully baked.

Our Perfect Pie Crust recipe produces this kind of shell. It calls for baking the weighted crust until the edges are golden, then removing the weights and continuing until the bottom and sides are evenly browned.

According to recent reports, and some pies need an even more substantial head start. Our Bourbon-Date Pecan Pie takes the crust to a dry golden finish before adding a filling that bakes for another 45–55 minutes.

The point isn’t that every custard pie needs the same color. It’s that the crust should be baked far enough that it won’t be left pale and doughy by the time the filling is done.

Bake the crust to a dark golden brown if you’re adding a no-bake filling, like a pudding or curd. You’re going for a toasty, burnished color, so don’t be gun-shy.

It has been revealed that because the filling won’t return to the oven, this is the crust’s one chance to bake all the way through. You want deep color across the entire bottom and up the sides—not just a dark rim surrounding a pale center. The pastry should look dry, crisp, and well browned, without any doughy or translucent spots.

According to recent reports, after removing the pie weights, continue baking until the shell is fully browned, checking frequently toward the end. Depending on the dough and oven temperature, that might take another 15–20 minutes or longer. Don’t pull it simply because the timer has gone off.

Our Cranberry Meringue Pie uses this approach: The crust is baked until golden and dry before the cranberry curd filling goes in. A fully baked shell develops a richer, toastier flavor and is better equipped to stand up to a moist filling.

Sources indicate that some recipes, including our pumpkin pie, call for brushing a thin layer of beaten egg onto the partially baked shell and returning it to the oven briefly to set. This, ostensibly, creates a barrier between the pastry and the filling, but not all bakers believe the hype.

According to recent reports, while it can be a useful extra precaution, it is by no means a universal requirement. If your recipe doesn’t call for it, there’s no need to add another step.

They’ll be here whenever you need them.

It has been revealed that cut this festive galette into little squares for a hearty appetizer, or serve sizeable wedges as a vegetarian main or standout side. It’s worth seeking out savoy cabbage, the ruffly sort that looks like lace. Ordinary green cabbage, which has a higher moisture content and flatter texture, doesn’t work here (we tried).

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

Whisk 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, ¼ tsp. baking powder, and 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour in a large bowl. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces, and rub in with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy). Add 10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea size). Make a well in the center and pour in ¼ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute. Knead dough in bowl just to bring together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn dough out onto a lightly dusted surface and sprinkle with all-purpose flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting dough with more flour as needed to prevent sticking. Pat into a ½"-thick disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

Do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

Industry observers note that when dough is almost done chilling, cut 1 medium head of savoy cabbage (1¾–2¼ lb.) in half and cut out triangular core at bottom; discard. Separate leaves and tear into pieces about the size of your palm. Transfer about half to a large bowl and set aside.

According to recent reports, melt 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 medium white or yellow onion, thinly sliced, and season generously with kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to turn translucent, about 5 minutes. Add remaining 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter and ¾ tsp. cumin seeds (if using) and cook until butter is melted. Add remaining cabbage leaves and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is translucent and lightly browned and cabbage is wilted, 18–22 minutes. Transfer to a large plate or a small baking sheet; chill in fridge or freezer until cool.

Place a rack in bottom third of oven; preheat to 400°. Whisk 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, ⅓ cup heavy cream, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a measuring glass to combine. Pour cream mixture over reserved raw cabbage leaves and toss with your hands to coat. Add 5 oz. Gruyère or sharp cheddar, coarsely grated, and toss again to combine.

Unwrap dough and roll out on a lightly floured sheet of parchment paper to a 13–14" round (some dough will extend beyond the parchment). Transfer on parchment paper to a baking sheet.

Spread cooked cabbage mixture over dough, leaving about a 1½" border around edges. Fold dough up and over filling, folding and tucking as needed to make a rustic border. Pile raw cabbage mixture on top of cooked cabbage mixture to make a dramatic heap. (It will look ridiculously high at first but will cook down when it bakes.).

Bake galette 25 minutes. Rotate baking sheet front to back, reduce heat to 375°, and bake until cabbage and crust are deep golden brown, 25–35 minutes. (If cabbage seems to be browning too much, reduce heat to 350° toward the end.) Let galette cool on baking sheet at least 1 hour and up to 4 hours before serving.

Industry observers note that do Ahead: Sautéed cabbage can be made 1 day ahead. Transfer to an airtight container and chill. Tightly wrap undressed raw cabbage in plastic and chill.

So go figure that at 21 years old, she’d find herself slap bang in the middle of the buzz. On Friday evening, as crowds swarmed Lexington Avenue and 59th Street to catch a glimpse of the breakthrough singer, Spiro was on hand to unveil the Bloomingdale’s holiday windows, created this season in collaboration with Ralph Lauren.

Something new has happened every single day. I can’t really keep up with it to be honest.”.

For her latest surreal career moment, the rising star donned a glossy red mackintosh coat from the Ralph Lauren archives, which she paired with black leather driving gloves and sky-high Louboutins—very in keeping with her youthful spin on a vintage-esque look that has been keeping her fans enthralled.

Though she’s not typically swayed by traditional Christmas songs, Spiro thrilled the audience with her one exception: “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas.” “The Frank Sinatra version, of course, with a little saxophone solo,” she noted. Those who had dutifully lined up to hear her smoky tones in real life were delighted when she also released into “Material Lover” and “Great Expectations.” Indeed, clips of the performance had already made it onto TikTok minutes after she departed the stage—fitting for a performer who was discovered on the platform as a teen.

Just after 7 p.m., Bloomingdale’s CEO Olivier Bron and Ralph Lauren chief branding and innovation officer David Lauren appeared to count down the window and lighting reveal. “We’re bringing two iconic New York brands together, who share the same appreciation for heritage, craftsmanship, and fashion,” Bron said. Behind them, vignettes provided an instant immersion into the plaid- and velvet-drenched world of Ralph Lauren during the holidays.

Recent findings suggest that post-show, guests, many of whom were dressed in Ralph Lauren, headed back into the department store to see the extent of the festive programming. At Forty Carrots, an UGG takeover sees specialty frozen yogurt on offer, while Roberto Coin has teamed up with Studio 59 on a new Italian menu. Around the store, which felt like an ode to a Love Actually scene, there was everything from a cappella trios and DJs to embroiderers busy at work personalizing presents.

As for Spiro, who had spent the previous night “singing her heart out” when she got to meet her idol Stevie Wonder at Madison Square Garden, she’s doing the holidays a little differently this year, and is set to spend the break in Japan ahead of kickstarting her next tour there in January. “It’s my first time going. I told them I’d play in a Starbucks if I had to, I just really wanted to get there.” With three tours, numerous awards highlights, and the festival circuit on the horizon, it’ll be a welcome chance to finally catch her breath.

In a recent development, “I’m really excited to just live a bit, outside of all of this, and grow,” she told Vogue. “I’m still super young. To be a really amazing artist, you’ve got to grow as a person so I’m excited to live, learn, and hopefully end up writing my next record at some point.”.

Gordon Ramsay has earned 17 Michelin stars throughout his career and still oversees nearly 100 restaurants. He also fronts prime-time TV franchises on both sides of the Atlantic and holds a couple of casual Guinness World Records (call him if you need to fillet a 10-pound fish in 1 minute five seconds).

This is a man who’s never met a goalpost he didn’t want to surpass. So it wasn’t entirely surprising when he posted a bare-chested shot of his six-pack to the grid earlier this month. What generated headlines was the occasion: his 60th birthday. “Gordon Ramsay thirst trap was not on my bingo card,” reads one comment. “My wife is on this app sir,” reads another.

At home in London, he reveals me the Insights section on his Instagram account, which reveals the photo has gotten over 62 million impressions. “It’s very strange,” he states. “I’ve had a lot of ribbing from my eldest daughter, Megan. She’s a police officer. She was like, ‘Dad, how can you do that to me?’ All her senior sergeants and officers were laughing and telling her to tell me they’re going for a run. They’re in their early 40s. And then my Royal Marines Commando son just sent me a message with: ‘WTF dad, what are you doing?’”.

Ramsay has been a pretty active guy for a while now, despite working in an industry typically associated with chaotic diets and zero time for exercise. He was a youth soccer player back in the day, before becoming a chef and then, in his 40s, going from weighing 252 pounds to competing in marathons and Ironmans.

All very impressive, but it’s even rarer to be this chiseled in your 60s (maintaining a low body fat percentage becomes harder as your testosterone and growth hormone production slows down). Read on to learn more about his preferred forms of cardio, his favorite pre-workout treat, and why he's established a daily cryotherapy routine. “I call it my freezer,” he says.

“15 minutes a day. It starts off with a quick two-minute stretch and 100 sit-ups every morning. Precore lifestyle is my ab cruncher thing—these things are fucking amazing, by the way. If I miss a day, then I have to punish it and do double the next day.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s not physically hard with substantial weights. These are 25 pounds. I’ll do a strength class once a week, 45 minutes. That’s it. Occasional push-ups and squats. No personal trainer.”.

“What’s helped tremendously, with no impact on any of the joints, is a lot of swimming. So I have an injury in my patella, my right knee, right now. So I just increased the swimming because that’s the only sport that can use every muscle in your body with zero impact. But cardio is off the charts.”.

Sources indicate that “I have a Zwift bike, so I jump on that for 45 minutes. There’s no impact on that. I’ll do that Monday, Wednesday, Friday and gear up for 90 minutes on a Sunday. If I wasn’t injured, I’d be doing three 5K runs again, Monday, Wednesday, Friday, 20-minute runs. I’ve got my 5K back down to 21 minutes. The dream is under 20. I was running at 19 and a half back in July. A 5K run is easy to do in the morning before work, it’s done within half an hour. Once I do that, I can gear up for either a two-hour bike on a Sunday or a 90-minute run. I alternate. So, one Sunday’s run, one Sunday’s bike.”.

Recent findings suggest that “10 years ago, I ruptured my Achilles. I invested in an AlterG, a beautiful running machine that takes your weight, so you get all the cardio you want and less impact on the joint.”.

In a recent development, “From the chef’s perspective, I call it my freezer. It’s the cryochamber. I do two sets of three minutes every morning. I try to go seven days a week in that thing, straight after [working out]. That is incredible. That’ll get up to like minus 160. For six minutes.”.

Sources indicate that “I’ve invested in a tiny little red-light therapy sauna outside in the garden, and it seats two of you, and so [I’ll do] half an hour of that, every other day. This doesn’t need to be done every day. Three times a week’s fine. So when I’m not running, the other day I’ll sit in that red-light therapy and spend 20 minutes, 30 minutes in there, which is brilliant.”.

Industry observers note that “The older you get, the more you have to stretch. I use a lot of bands. And so after sitting and stretching, I had those incredible bands where you lift your feet up and pull and stretch. 5 minutes is always a nice stretch before you [work out] and then 10 minutes stretch after that. I’ve never been to a yoga class in my life.”.

“I’m big on oatmeal for breakfast, Monday to Friday. I indulge Saturday, Sunday. I will do [oatmeal with] blueberry compote, caramelized banana for my potassium, and then fresh blueberries on top with some—it sounds weird, but it’s delicious—hot honey.”.

“I have my friends at Precision. I’ll do one of their gels before I start that 5K, a protein gel, 30 grams, and then that sees me through the whole 45-minute routine. Coffee is just a full-fat, flat white, extra hot. Extra hot means I can sip it slowly. I cut out a lot of dairy, a lot of butter, a lot of cream. And so that treat in the morning with a flat white is that sort of, ‘I’ve earned this shit.’”.

“I don’t overstress on that because I stay fit. I monitor what I eat, but if anything, I’ll do smaller portions now. I’ll involve a lot of spinach, involve a lot of salmon, chicken, especially thighs. We’re just smart with less cream, less butter intake. And then when we travel, we just keep it light.”.

It has been revealed that our classic pecan pie recipe has no chocolate chips, no booze, and no hard-to-find ingredients. Instead of focusing on embellishments, we focused on what matters most: the deep flavor of toasted pecans, a caramelly custard, and a buttery, flaky pie crust.

Brown sugar and a spoonful of dark molasses add depth to the filling, while toasting the pecans before incorporating them makes their flavor stand out and their texture more robust. Blind baking the crust—baking it before adding the filling—helps keep the bottom crisp beneath the gooey custard.

When the pie comes out of the oven, the edges should be set and slightly puffed, but the center should still wobble like Jell-O. It will continue to set as it cools, so resist slicing too soon. Serve it all on its own, or gild it with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.

Can I make this pecan pie without corn syrup?

According to recent reports, yes. Corn syrup gives this classic pie its perfectly gooey texture, but there are alternatives. Brown rice syrup will add a toasty flavor and can be used in equal parts. Golden syrup, honey, and maple syrup are all too sweet and will change the pie’s flavor and texture.

For a pie developed without any syrup, try our Bourbon-Date Pecan Pie.

Can I use chopped pecans instead of halves?

According to recent reports, yes. We love the crunch you get from pecan halves, but if you’re a chopped pecan person, use about 225 g in place of the 2 cups of halves. Watch closely when toasting; chopped pecans will need less time in the oven.

Can I make pecan pie ahead of time?

Industry observers note that yes—bake the pie a day ahead and refrigerate it. Let it cool on a rack for up to 2 hours, then transfer it to the refrigerator to finish cooling before covering. To get a head start on the pastry, refrigerate the dough for up to 3 days or freeze it for up to 2 months.

With motor running, drizzle in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar and 5½ Tbsp. ice water and pulse until dough is still crumbly but just holds together when squeezed (add 1 tsp. water at a time if necessary, but be careful not to overwork dough).

Turn out dough onto a work surface. Knead 1–2 times, pressing just to incorporate any shaggy pieces. Flatten into a 6"-wide disk. Wrap with plastic wrap and chill at least 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 425°. Roll out dough on a lightly floured work surface to a 14" round. Transfer to a 9" pie pan. Pick up edges and allow dough to slump down into dish, letting excess dough hang over dish. Trim, leaving about a 1" overhang. Fold overhang under; pinch and crimp. Chill 30 minutes.

Industry observers note that line dough with parchment paper or foil, leaving some overhang. Fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake until crust is dry around the edges and just beginning to lightly brown, 25–35 minutes. Carefully remove parchment and weights and reduce oven temperature to 350°. Bake until crust is set and beginning to brown in the center, 10–15 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack and let cool.

Alas, they are the mundane mechanics of even the most thrilling of married lives. Soon after a ring is on the finger, many couples are now discussing prenups—and it’s a topic that brings up unglamorous realities.

No, the administrative process of a prenup isn’t inherently romantic, and let’s not pretend it is. But what it does for the relationship—laying everything bare with radical honesty—is deeply romantic.

Sources indicate that “I think navigating something that’s challenging in a relationship and coming out of it aligned is romantic, sexy, and empowering,” notes Ashley Hesseltine. The co-host of Girls Gotta Eat spoke openly about choosing to have a prenuptial agreement with her now husband. “But I will not lie. The process of a prenup is inherently annoying, unsexy, and invasive. And it’s admin.”.

Wedding planning has a way of sweeping us up into a whirlwind of floral arrangements, seating charts, and linen swatches. Conversations about money, family expectations, and core values naturally come to the forefront next to celebrations.

Luxury wedding planner JoAnn Gregoli agrees that pausing and zooming out to address a prenuptial agreement and the structural foundation of your partnership before you even start picking a venue makes the whole planning process all the more clear. “Marriage isn’t only about romance; it’s also about finances, property, obligations, and decision-making,” she claims. “When a couple confronts the subject together, they feel more like they’re entering the marriage as a team and not as a dictatorship.”.

You’ve likely already experienced that deep feeling of intimacy with your partner after an exceptionally vulnerable conversation with them. This is just like that. Afterwards, wedding planning transforms from a period of financial tension into one of deep alignment.

It has been revealed that it helps, but there’s no requirement to execute a 30-page legal document to reap the emotional rewards of the prenup talk. Some value lies in the vulnerability required to have the conversation at all.

Therapist and author Israa Nasir notes that money remains one of the ultimate taboos in modern relationships, often carrying hidden emotional baggage. “Constructive and supportive conversations can reveal parts of yourself that you otherwise might not—deeper insecurities, past experiences with financial trauma, childhood scarcity, and your relationship with money,” she says. “If your partner doesn’t understand why you behave a certain way about money, it’s harder for them to have empathy for you.”.

Recent findings suggest that it may feel like you’re setting up transactional boundaries or betting against your longevity. But in essence, it’s an exercise in radical honesty. Approaching your partner with curiosity rather than judgment is a quick way to turn a wobbly topic fraught with anxiety into a brick in your foundation.

Nobody’s excited about asking their partner about student loans or retirement accounts. It may feel daunting. That’s completely normal.

Recent findings suggest that start small, and don’t put the pressure on this having to be one significant conversation. The first chat can just be about getting their thoughts on prenups in general. Then, you can talk about your thoughts on how you want to manage finances in your relationship. Finally, when you’re ready, you can start diving into assets and what each person wants to walk away with.

In a recent development, the time-old advice of there being no such thing as too much communication stands here. You can even talk about how you want to enter this conversation in a way that might make both of you feel the most comfortable. Agree to enter the discussion with empathy, zero judgment, and positive intent.

Remind yourself that you can frame this discussion around shared goals and mutual care.

Here are a couple of conversation starters:.

It has been revealed that I’m fairly certain nobody gets married to get divorced. If it does happen, state laws dictate what happens to you both. Letting state statutes dictate your shared destiny? Not romantic. An act of mutual protection? Maybe even chivalrous.

It has been revealed that family and divorce mediator Aswini Puvitharan highlights how modern prenups are moving away from traditional adversarial mindsets. “Prenups are often introduced as ‘How do I protect what’s mine?’ but the better starting point is ‘What would fairness and financial security look like for both of us?’ The more thoughtful prenups today reflect deep care—providing housing, financial support, or protecting someone who takes a career break to raise children.”.

In a recent development, protection from potential bitterness or future legal chaos is inherently loving. “It should feel like you and your partner against the prenup, not you and your partner against each other,” says Hesseltine. “It’s an insurance policy you’re probably never going to use, and if you were strong enough to figure this out together in a healthy way, chances are you’ll never need it.”.

A Brief Guide to Grand Theft Auto VI’s Nike Sneaker Dupes

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, GTA 6 is finally out, which means we’ve got some in-game sneaker shopping to do.
  • In a recent development, even the name is a joke.
  • The Eris Rise Low is the obvious starting point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, GTA 6 is finally out, which means we’ve got some in-game sneaker shopping to do. We’d already spotted Air Force 1 dupes in the trailers, but now that we can finally play the long-awaited masterpiece itself, we’re taking a closer look at what else is on the shelves. There are tons of different sneaker stores sprinkled throughout the game, and Eris—Rockstar’s fictional answer to Nike—has given us a lot to work through.

In a recent development, even the name is a joke. Nike takes its name from the Greek goddess of victory, while Eris is the goddess of strife and discord—an appropriate choice for kicks you might buy with money from an armed robbery. The Swoosh has been replaced with a pointier, upside-down logo, and plenty of the sneakers baring the mark are instantly recognizable.

The Eris Rise Low is the obvious starting point. It’s the game’s AF1 equivalent, complete with the familiar paneled upper, perforated toebox, and a massive, beefy sole underfoot. The Eris Strife 360, meanwhile, looks straight out of the Air Max 97 catalog. There’s the rippling upper, rounded toe, and long cushioning window underneath. Designed by Christian Tresser and released in 1997, the IRL sneaker’s silhouette took inspiration from water ripples, while the OG “Silver Bullet” finish drew on mountain bike components. Eris keeps enough of that shape for you to be able to spot it from across the shop.

Off-White x Nike Air Max 97 ‘White’.

Some versions get even more specific. There’s a white-and-orange Strife 360, for example, with oversized branding, contrasting lace loops, and printed side text that recalls Off-White’s own Air Max 97s. It isn’t a straight one-to-one recreation, but the reference feels pretty clear. An apparent take on the Off-White Air Force 1 Mid also appeared in the teasers. Someone at Rockstar is clearly a fan of Virgil Abloh’s work.

Then there’s the Eris Strife 90, with pairs that borrow heavily from the Air Max 90 “Infrared.” The bright red accents and sharp, aggressive lines are all there, with one colorway even adding black scribbles across the overlays.

Recent findings suggest that arguably the most iconic signature shoe of all time, the Air Jordan 1, gets a look in the game as well. The Eris Rook 1 High comes in leather and suede variations, with a tall ankle collar and laces running almost all the way up. There’s a black-and-white pair that swaps Jordan branding for an Eris basketball graphic on the tongue. You’ve probably got something quite similar in your closet at home.

Air Jordan 1 High OG ‘Yin Yang’.

According to recent reports, the Eris Cross Trainers are, well, harder to pin down. Available in several colorways, they have a mesh base and leather overlays. One white-and-gray version gets bright green hits that nod to Nike’s signature “Volt” hue. The simpler construction puts it closer to an older Nike runner, somewhere around MD Runner 2 territory, than a direct Zoom Vomero 5 or V5 Rnr copy. And for those times that tying laces feels like too much work, there are the very appropriately named Eris Basic Slides. The broad branded strap and flat footbed are very Nike Benassi.

It has been revealed that there are different versions to consider, too. “Origins” go all-white, while “Elite” options are matte and all-black. So if you‘ve found a silhouette you like, you can still spend another 10 minutes deciding which version works with your trousers. A problem we were hoping to leave outside the game.

According to recent reports, it gives you an idea of just how much there is in GTA 6. The older games let you change your clothes, but here you’re choosing between different colorways, materials, and versions of individual shoes. And Eris is only one part of it: There are clothes and accessories that look like takes on Stüssy, Loewe, Chrome Hearts, and Louis Vuitton, too. You could spend a fair bit of time getting dressed before you get anything else done.

Sources indicate that we’ve waited this long to play the game. A few more minutes in the sneaker shop before you really get going on missions won’t hurt.

A version of the story originally appeared on British GQ.

Will There Be Another Hunger Games Movie—and Which Character Will It Be About?

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that sunrise on the Reaping details the story of Haymitch Abernathy’s Hunger Games and sets the stage for his involvement in overthrowing President Snow in the Second Rebellion, but there are so many stories within Suzanne Collins’s rich universe that are begging to be told.
  • Recent findings suggest that “It’s interesting, because it’s always a surprise when she writes a book.
  • According to recent reports, here’s everything we know so far about a possible next installment in the Hunger Games movie franchise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sunrise on the Reaping details the story of Haymitch Abernathy’s Hunger Games and sets the stage for his involvement in overthrowing President Snow in the Second Rebellion, but there are so many stories within Suzanne Collins’s rich universe that are begging to be told. But is there another movie in the works, and if so, who would it be about?

Recent findings suggest that “It’s interesting, because it’s always a surprise when she writes a book. She never tells us ahead of time, and Suzanne always surprises me and Nina [Jacobson], the [franchise’s] producer, with usually a pretty close-to-finished manuscript,” Francis Lawrence, Sunrise on the Reaping’s director, told ELLE in a September 2026 interview.

According to recent reports, here’s everything we know so far about a possible next installment in the Hunger Games movie franchise. Warning: Book and movie spoilers ahead.

There are presently no details about any future Hunger Games movies, but if Collins releases another book in the series, that has the potential to change.

It’s possible that Lawrence and Jacobson would return if another film is greenlit. Lawrence has directed every movie in the franchise since Catching Fire, and Jacobson has produced each installment.

There have been no details on a plot for a future Hunger Games movie, but there are already more than a few popular characters and topics that fans would like to see, should the franchise receive another installment:.

First introduced in Catching Fire with the arrival of the Third Quarter Quell, Finnick quickly became a fan favorite thanks to his confidence and charm, which was only amplified when Sam Claflin starred as the victor in the book’s respective movie adaptation. But Finnick’s backstory is much more tragic than meets the eye. After becoming the youngest Hunger Games winner at 14, he was forced into sex trafficking and prostitution by President Snow.

Instead of perpetuating that pain, Finnick chose to protect those around him, notably his mentor, Mags, his romantic interest, Annie Cresta, and Katniss. If Finnick gets a movie of his own, it would provide details on the 65th Hunger Games, which takes place nine years before Katniss volunteers to participate in the 74th Hunger Games.

It has been revealed that also introduced with the Third Quarter Quell, Joanna (played by Jena Malone) became a beloved character in the franchise for entirely different reasons than Finnick. She’s outspoken, fearless, publicly opposes the Capitol and President Snow, and is never afraid to make others uncomfortable (see: the infamous Catching Fire scene in which she undresses in front of Katniss and Peeta in the elevator)—and she has every reason to be that way.

In a recent development, joanna won the 71st Hunger Games by pretending to be a “sniveling, cowardly fool” and later proving that she was incredibly skilled with an axe. Like Finnick, she was also forced into sex trafficking by President Snow, who killed or tortured her loved ones if she didn’t cooperate; by the time fans meet her in the Third Quarter Quell, all of her loved ones are dead. A movie could dive into Joanna’s strategy for the 71st games, and how she became radicalized enough to participate in the Second Rebellion.

Sources indicate that A movie about Mags could offer a unique bridge between the events that took place in Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, President Snow’s ascent to power, and the revamping of the Hunger Games system as we know it. Mags won the 11th Hunger Games—a year after Lucy Gray did in Songbirds, though she was later erased from history—and was the first victor in the history of the games to experience monetary prizes and life in the Victor’s Village, in addition to being the first to do a Victory Tour after winning, changes that were included at Snow’s insistence.

In Sunrise on the Reaping, Mags (Lili Taylor) works as Haymitch and Maysilee’s mentor, offering him a shoulder to cry on after Louella McCoy dies. By the Third Quarter Quell, Finnick revealed that Mags (Lynn Cohen) essentially raised him, and she volunteers in Annie’s place, ultimately sacrificing herself in Catching Fire when it becomes too difficult for her to move on.

Several clues are given about Wiress’s time in the 49th Hunger Games when fans meet her in Sunrise on the Reaping. During her games, the arena was completely covered in reflective and shiny mirror-like surfaces, making it difficult for the tributes to fight their way out of the arena. She won her games by hiding out in a blind spot until it was over and did not kill a single tribute. Visually, a movie with Wiress’s arena could be a feast for the eyes.

Wiress (Maya Hawke) appears in Sunrise on the Reaping and acts as Haymitch and Maysilee’s mentor; she later returns to the franchise in Catching Fire (Amanda Plummer) and uncovers that the arena works like a clock, inspiring the rebellion to make a newly introduced proposal to break the arena.

Plutarch, a Capitol citizen with decades of wealth and influence to his name, has never been selected to participate in any Hunger Games, but his presence is deeply felt within the franchise.

According to recent reports, in Sunrise on the Reaping, he (Jesse Plemmons) works on props for District 12 and lets Haymitch know that he’s actively working on the rebellion by giving Haymitch tips on how he can advance in the games and show resistance to the Capitol. While Haymitch is unsuccessful at being the spark needed to kick-start the Second Rebellion, Heavensbee stays on and works his way up to head gamemaker by the 74th Hunger Games with Katniss; he ends up becoming the brains behind the rebellion and leads it to victory. A Plutarch prequel could give longtime fans of the franchise a look into how a character with such proximity to the Capitol could become turned against it.

While fans are always hoping that Collins expands upon the existing Hunger Games characters, some are also looking for a fresh story that details a Hunger Games with a brand-newly introduced tribute that has no existing backstory in the franchise. Similarly, the exact events of The Dark Days—also known as the First Rebellion, which drove District 13 underground and started the Hunger Games after their years-long civil war with the Capitol—were never shown on-screen, and that could be a compelling story to give context to the Second Rebellion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in the midst of a rich meal, something fresh and acidic keeps your taste buds awake. Where lettuce splashed with vinaigrette can feel like an afterthought, a juicy, savory-slanting pear salad is worth making room for on a plate full of turkey and cornbread. This is the antithesis of the haphazardly chunked together fruit salads you find at the supermarket for a brunch or dessert spread. Keep the focus on crisp-tart pears—apples also work—and it’s a welcome accompaniment to the other hearty dishes. Sliced razor-thin (use a mandoline) and fanned out on a platter, the fruit acts as an edible canvas for wisps of cheese and clusters of honey-roasted seeds. Leftovers (if you have any, of course) are delightful spooned over a well-toasted and buttered slice of multigrain bread the next day.

Pick firm green pears (Bartlett and Anjou are fair game; use Asian pears in a pinch) to ensure they hold their shape once sliced—even a little underripe is better than slightly over. After slicing, have a taste: If they are very tart, add 1 tsp. honey to the dressing; if fairly sweet, skip it.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

Recent findings suggest that preheat oven to 325°. Whisk 3 Tbsp. honey, 1 tsp. garlic powder, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, and ¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl to combine. Add 1 cup raw sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds (pepitas), and/or coarsely crushed raw nuts (such as walnuts, almonds, and/or hazelnuts) and stir to coat. Spread out in a single layer on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet; reserve bowl.

Bake seed mixture until golden brown, 12–14 minutes. (Honey mixture will puff up a bit but will deflate when you stir.) Toss honey-roasted seeds, then let cool. Toss again just to break up.

Whisk 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp. Dijon mustard, a pinch of kosher salt, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in reserved bowl. Add 2 lb. firm green pears (such as Bartlett and/or Anjou; about 4 large), cored, thinly sliced, to dressing and gently toss to coat.

In a recent development, arrange pears on a large flat platter. Scatter honey-roasted seeds over and top with 2 oz. Parmesan, aged white cheddar, or Manchego cheese, shaved.

It has been revealed that do Ahead: Honey-roasted seeds can be made 6 hours ahead. Store at room temperature.
